papers.abstract: We investigate effects of longitudinally varying nonlinearity on periodically distributed amplification systems in optical fibres. Emphasis is made on configurations in which the nonlinear coefficient exponentially grows or decays along the propagation distance, while the group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) coefficient is held constant. Such systems are of practical relevance to the design of highly efficient nonlinear devices, including broadband light sources and advanced amplification schemes, where precise management of the interplay between the GVD, nonlinearity, and gain is essential. Adopting the known generic integrability condition, we derive exact analytical expressions for the evolution of the optical field in the presence of the tailored nonlinearity profiles and periodically distributed gain. The resulting periodic wavetrain solutions and their long-wave limit in the form of bright and dark solitons provide insight into the controlled enhancement or suppression of nonlinear effects under realistic amplification conditions. The robustness of these solutions is examined by introducing finite perturbations and directly evaluating their effects on the corresponding intensity profiles. The structural stability of solutions against deviations from the integrability condition is demonstrated too. Outcomes of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the nonlinear pulse dynamics in engineered gain-managed fibres and offer guidance for the development of novel optical systems, where the spatial distribution of the nonlinearity is exploited to optimise the performance.

papers.title: Exothermic Higgs portal: from LUX-ZEPLIN recoil to Gamma Rays
papers.abstract: We show that a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM) by a single complex scalar $φ$ provides a viable inelastic exothermic, thermal relic, interpretation of the recently reported nuclear-recoil candidate from LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ). The mass terms and Higgs-portal interactions split $φ$ into two nearly degenerate real scalars, $φ_{1,2}$. For mass-splitting of a few hundred keV, $φ_2$ is cosmologically long-lived and the two states have comparable relic abundances. Taking $φ_{1,2}$ masses to be $\sim100\,$GeV, with off-diagonal Higgs coupling fixed by relic abundance, the exothermic down-scattering yields an order-one event expectation for the LZ exposure, without relying on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter velocity distribution required in endothermic scenarios. This scenario can be tested using different nuclear targets and with indirect dark matter searches: $φ_2\toφ_1γγ$ decays give a broad sub-MeV photon continuum that can be probed by INTEGRAL/SPI and COSI; $φ_1φ_2$ annihilation produces a GeV-scale continuum, extending up to $\sim$100 GeV, that is probed by Fermi-LAT observations of dwarf galaxies; current CMB constraints are satisfied and annihilation among dark matter particles captured in the Sun is strongly suppressed. Next-generation experiments could probe correlated scattering, decay, and annihilation signatures of this thermal Higgs-portal scenario.

papers.title: Lower Bounds on Inference Complexity for Polyak-Ruppert Averaged Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp lower bounds for Gaussian approximation of Polyak-Ruppert averaged stochastic gradient descent with polynomially decreasing step sizes. For every fixed exponent $γ\in(1/2,1)$, a single one-dimensional smooth, strongly convex example has approximation error with the limiting variance of order $n^{1/2-γ}+n^{γ-1}$ in Kolmogorov and convex distances. This matches the existing upper bound throughout the range of $γ$. The nonlinear bias contributes $n^{1/2-γ}$ even when the Gaussian reference uses the finite linearized variance. We also derive a lower bound of order $n^{-(1-γ)/2}$ for the relative mean error of estimating the limiting variance from one SGD trajectory, uniformly over a scalar quadratic family. With the limiting variance known, achieving approximation error $\varepsilon$ on this example takes order $\varepsilon^{-4}$ iterations for the best choice $γ=3/4$. Achieving both Gaussian approximation and relative mean variance-estimation errors at most $\varepsilon$ uniformly over the model class requires at least order $\varepsilon^{-6}$ iterations for every fixed $γ$.

papers.title: Behavior of the zero modes in the Light-front for pseudo scalar particles: pion case
papers.abstract: Light-front Quantum Field Theory (LFQFT) stands as an optimal framework for delving into the intricate substructure of hadronic bound states. In this study, we employ a Light-Front Constituent Quark Model (LFCQM) to investigate the pion's internal structure. This model has previously demonstrated significant success in describing the properties of pseudoscalar mesons. A crucial consideration within the light-front formalism is the dependence on the chosen reference frame, stemming from the explicit breaking of covariance. Herein, we meticulously analyze the contribution of zero modes to the pion's electromagnetic current. Subsequently, we explore the impact of these zero modes on observable quantities, including electromagnetic form factors, the pion's electromagnetic radius, and its weak decay constant, $f_π$. Furthermore, we comprehensively investigate the behavior of zero modes and their dependence on both the momentum transfer, $Q^2$, and the model's intrinsic parameters, such as constituent quark masses ($m_{(q,\bar{q})}$) and the regulator mass ($m_R$). Our findings reveal a substantial dependence of light-front zero modes on the specific frame employed for the calculation of the electromagnetic current. Interestingly, we observe that the maximal contribution of the zero mode occurs at a specific four-momentum transfer, denoted as $Q^2 = -q^2 = q_Z^{2(Max.)}$.
authors: J. Pacheco B. C. de melo

papers.title: Selective inference for pruned interaction trees with known unequal variances in randomized trials
papers.abstract: Interaction trees reuse outcomes to discover treatment-effect heterogeneity, complicating inference after growth and pruning. We develop selective inference for generalized least-squares (GLS) interaction trees with a common covariate basis and known unequal variances. Under a conditional Gaussian model with positive diagonal covariance, weighted orthogonality reduces survival under additive fixed-penalty pruning to one quadratic inequality supplementing the growth event. This yields exact finite-sample conditional tests and confidence intervals, with retained-path and complete-tree inference agreeing on compatible sections. Under causal identification and a correct reference prognosis, the pruning-invariant GLS target is a signed finite-design weighted contrast of conditional average treatment effects. Simulations at $n=100,200,400,800$ and maximum depths one to three search all adjacent-observation midpoints, support calibration and demonstrate over-rejection when pruning survival is omitted. Compared with a 50:50 honest procedure, full-data learning improves reference-split recovery in some small-sample settings. Root-level median intervals can be shorter, while deep-node intervals and upper tails can be much wider; these comparisons concern each procedure's selected targets. Estimating a common scale with the variance ratio fixed produces modest changes in Selective coverage in the settings examined, without extending the exact guarantee. An exploratory ACTG 175 analysis provides a working-model illustration with estimated arm variances.

papers.title: Extended Onsager's variational principle for nonlinear chemical reaction kinetics in active matter
papers.abstract: Onsager's variational principle (OVP) constructs dissipative dynamics from free energy, dissipation, and input power, but deterministic rate laws alone do not identify fluctuations or chemical fuel consumption. We examine these distinctions for nonlinear reaction kinetics in active matter. Comparing Gaussian diffusion and Poisson reaction events clarifies when statistical fluctuations match a physical Rayleighian: the reaction dissipation potential must be consistent with counting statistics, local detailed balance links rate bias to chemical affinity, and kinetic scales remain constitutive inputs. Under these conditions, the normalized Rayleighian excess gives the leading rate-fluctuation cost in the frozen-state, many-event regime. Three models illustrate the consequences. Spatially uniform reactions exhibit protocol-dependent nonreciprocal response compatible with fixed-state OVP; different Rayleighian representations can select the same rate without specifying the same fluctuations. In an active emulsion, a finite fuel pool accounts for free-energy transfer and dissolution of a chemically maintained domain after replenishment stops. In a membrane-cytosol model, distinct reaction-channel realizations yield identical protein-density trajectories but different chemical input power. Under a separate kinetic assumption, an exact total-density equation still requires an initial rate and does not determine chemical work or fluctuations. These results clarify the physical and statistical inputs required for constructing reaction-transport models and interpreting their fluctuations.

papers.title: Nonlinear Physics and Self-Organized Criticality in Astrophysics
papers.abstract: The definition of self-organized criticality (SOC) is ambiguous and controversial. Here we discuss the nonlinear physics of six basic SOC definitions, such as: phase transitions, fractal structures, power laws, SOC contingency, exponential growth, and diffusive decay. Statistics of SOC events or avalanche processes can be inferred from their size distributions, or from their spatio-temporal evolution.

papers.title: Direct imaging of the Ni $e_g$ hole orbitals in the bilayer nickelate La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$
papers.abstract: Models of unconventional superconductivity in cuprates and nickelates depend sensitively on the distribution of valence electrons among the $d$ orbitals. But accurately determining the orbital electron or hole occupations in these systems remains a difficult and unresolved task. Here, using $s$-core-level non-resonant inelastic x-ray scattering at the Ni $M_1$ edge, we determine the angular distribution of the Ni $3d$ holes in a single crystal of La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$. Our results demonstrate that the hole occupation ratio $\hz/\hx = 0.94\pm0.06$, thus significantly above the expected value of $2/3$ for a filled $d_{z^2}$ orbitals models and close to value expected in a Hund's-coupling picture. Our results support superconductivity scenarios in which both $e_g$ orbitals contribute to the electron-pairing mechanism in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$.

papers.title: LH$μ$C Concept: Energy-Frontier Antimuon-Proton Collisions at CERN
papers.abstract: The concept of the LH$μ$C, an energy-frontier antimuon-proton collider based on the HL-LHC, is presented. After recalling why energy-frontier lepton-hadron colliders are indispensable as QCD explorers and reviewing the history of muon-proton collider proposals, two ways of realising $μp$ collisions at the LHC are compared: with muon-collider beams and with ultra-cold $μ^+$ beams as proposed for $μ$TRISTAN. For the latter, a $μ$TRISTAN-type booster and the re-use of the LHeC energy-recovery-linac tunnel are discussed; colliding 1 TeV antimuons with 7 TeV protons gives $\sqrt{s}=5.3$ TeV and peak luminosities of $8.8\times10^{33}$ and $7.2\times10^{33}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, respectively. The detector concept and the physics potential, including searches for colour-octet muons and R-parity-violating squarks, are discussed together with the main challenges.

papers.title: Optimal Fan-Out and Break-Even Routing Loss in Waveguide-Integrated Ge-on-Si SPAD Arrays
papers.abstract: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts. We quantify this trade-off with the asymptotic count-based information rate, which prices dark counts and dead time in one unit and is attained by an optimally weighted moment estimator. For a non-paralyzable pixel, the information per pre-dead-time signal event peaks at a signal rate $y^*=\sqrt{D(D+1/τ)}$ with exact efficiency $(\sqrt{1+Dτ}-\sqrt{Dτ})^2$, which sets the optimal fan-out and a critical flux above which equal splitting is optimal. We then compare four routing architectures on 64 simulated 16-pixel arrays: an equal passive tree, static trees (uncalibrated, and an idealized calibration-informed benchmark), an ideal programmable tree, and a thermo-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) tree with 1.32 dB excess loss. Ideal programmability gains up to 15.9 dB over equal splitting at low flux. At one known flux, however, the calibrated static splitter beats the MZI tree by 0.14-2.7 dB, and the penalty tends to twice the excess loss when dark counts dominate. In ensemble-median worst-case regret, the MZI tree breaks even only for flux windows wider than 2.55 decades, and not within six decades above about 3.4 dB excess loss. Event-level Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the count statistics and the predicted estimator variances within bootstrap confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses cover dark-count level, heterogeneity, detector model and random seed. All results are simulations with representative literature parameters.

papers.title: Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
papers.abstract: Liouvillian skin effects are usually associated with dissipation whose rates favor unidirectional flow. In this work, we show that directional edge localization can emerge even when population exchange between sites is exactly balanced, with a single tunable phase parameter $α$ deciding their direction and a dual winding structure deciding their nature. Although this number-conserving bath is known for eigenstate selection, we demonstrate here that its phase controls a steady current, which Hamiltonian hopping converts to directional edge localization. Further, we study the spectral winding structure by independently twisting the left (ket) and right (bra) vector indices of the density matrix, revealing two distinct windings whose relationship is dictated by an antiunitary mirror symmetry. Nearest-neighbor jump operators break this symmetry: both windings coincide, giving rise to a common spectral winding $W_0(α)=\pm1$, producing a unipolar skin effect in which the density accumulates at a specific edge. However, next nearest neighbor jump preserve it. The two windings are forced to be opposite, and the ket and bra are pushed to opposite edges, giving a bipolar skin effect of coherences present in eigenmodes, without edge localization of the density in the steady state. Remarkably, in a dimerized chain the phase-controlled density skin effect gives the steady-state zero modes a size-independent weight at the skin edge, accompanied by a kink at the topological transition. In addition, the relaxation time grows linearly with the system size, however at specific phases $α$ where the jump operators are rendered Hermitian, edge-localized eigenmodes with skin character coexist with diffusive relaxation.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Assisted Fast Beam Alignment for mmWave MIMO Networks
papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication relies on directional beam sweeping for initial access, which incurs substantial latency and signaling overhead as antenna arrays grow large and deployments become denser. Machine-learning-based beam prediction can reduce this overhead, but its effectiveness depends on training data that accurately reflects the deployment environment, a requirement that is difficult to meet in practice. This paper presents a latency-aware beam management architecture that integrates digital-twin-assisted prediction, regionbased localization, weighted ensemble learning, and explainability-driven beam pruning into a unified framework. A digital twin (DT) generates site-specific ray-traced channel knowledge offline, enabling environment-aware beam prediction without exhaustive real-world measurements and supporting both initial access and beam tracking. The proposed ensemble learning scheme combines a base classifier and a specialist classifier through reliability-weighted fusion to improve prediction accuracy and robustness, while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based attribution pruning reduces the beam codebook to a small subset of the most informative beams for beam allocation. To capture the distributional mismatch between the DT and real-world environments: the network was trained on imperfect digital-twin data but evaluated on real-world surrobase data. Results show that the proposed method achieves 96.80% top-1 and 98.36% top-3 beam prediction accuracy, while reducing over-the-air sounding overhead by nearly an order of magnitude relative to exhaustive sweeping, outperforming convolutional and deep neural network baselines from prior work.

papers.title: Minimum-Norm Interpolation in Weighted Variation Spaces: Direct and Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We study minimum-norm interpolation in weighted variation spaces generated by ReLU$^s$ ridge functions on the unit ball, where $s$ is a positive integer. For a target $f$ in the weighted variation space and a node set with sufficiently small fill distance $h$, every minimum-norm interpolant satisfies the direct bound $\|f-\mathscr{I}_{X_h}f\|_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}h^{(2s+1)/4}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$. Under a boundary separation condition on the nodes, we construct a matching lower bound for the worst-case interpolation error. For the inverse problem, we introduce dual certificates and derive an estimate analogous to a Bernstein inequality. Under suitable upper bounds on dictionary size and spectral lower bounds for the atomic Gram matrices, sufficiently fast $L_2$ convergence of minimum-norm interpolants along geometrically decreasing fill distances implies that the target belongs to $\mathcal{V}_s$. As a byproduct, the best $L_2$ approximation error $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}$ for shallow ReLU$^s$ networks of width at most $n$ satisfies $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}n^{-1/2-(2s+1)/(2d)}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, with the weighted atomic cost of an approximating network bounded by a constant multiple of $\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, independently of $n$.

papers.title: Comment on "Zero temperature, degenerate fermion stars" [S. Boatto, M.B. Paranjape, V. Pessanha, C.A.D. Zarro. ArXiv: 2609.20950]
papers.abstract: In contrast to S. Boatto et al. \cite{Boat}, the degree of compactification or compactness is clarified for the self-gravitating spheric star of fermionic matter.

papers.title: From Gaussian to stable and back: Non-Pareto points in growing dimension
papers.abstract: We study the number of non-Pareto points in two high-dimensional models: a homogeneous Poisson point process and a fixed-size sample of independent uniform points in the unit cube. A point is non-Pareto if some other sample point is coordinatewise less than or equal to it. As the dimension grows on the logarithmic scale of the intensity or sample size, the asymptotic behavior exhibits a surprising sequence of transitions: from Gaussian to stable fluctuations, back to Gaussian, then to a Poisson limit at the sparsity threshold, followed by the eventual disappearance of non-Pareto points. We identify the critical thresholds, normalizations, and limiting laws in both models. Notably, the return to Gaussianity occurs while the stability index remains strictly below $2$ and is driven by a change in the dominant fluctuation mechanism. Moreover, in part of the returning Gaussian regime, the natural normalization is the square root of the expected count rather than its standard deviation. At the stable--Gaussian transition, the two mechanisms can coexist, giving rise to a sum of independent stable and Gaussian random variables.

papers.title: New Scaling Relations for Nucleons in Three-Nucleon Short-Range Correlations
papers.abstract: The search for three nucleon short range correlations~(3N- SRCs) in nuclei is one of the intensive areas of research in high density nuclear physics. It is in part motivated by the prediction of the above two-solar mass neutron stars based on 3N short-range forces and the subsequent observation of such stars. The 3N-SRCs serve as a "laboratory" for probing the dynamics of largely unknown irreducible 3N-forces. However, the identification of 3N-SRCs in high energy nuclear processes is still elusive making the prospects of their investigation problematic. In this work we introduced new dynamical parameters for 2N- and 3N- SRCs, $β_{2N}$ and $β_{3N}$ respectively, which characterize the strength of SRCs beyond combinatorial counting of nucleons in SRCs. For 2N-SRCs the introduction of $β_{2N}$ parameter resulted in a previously known and experimentally verified relation for proton and neutron momentum distributions in 2N-SRCS. For 3N-SRCs the $β_{3N}$ parameter allowed to factorize momentum distributions of nucleons in the correlation resulting in a prediction of a new scaling relation between proton and neutron momentum distributions in 3N SRCs. This relation, if valid gives a new venue for identification of 3N-SRCs in electro-nuclear processes. Even though the obtained scaling relation is relevant in the relativistic domain, the possibility of separating center of mass motion of SRCs on the light-front allows to check the validity of predicted scaling using non-relativistic ab-initio wave functions. We found surprisingly reasonable confirmation of our prediction analyzing ab-initio wave functions of nuclei in the range $3\le A\le 12$. This indicates the robustness of the scaling relation and opens up a new direction in searching for 3N-SRCs experimentally.

papers.title: Chiral Unidirectional Resonances Enabled by Complete Coherent Radiation Control
papers.abstract: Optical resonances are commonly characterized by their quality factors, while their radiation exhibits richer properties associated with polarization and directional selectivity. Chiral and unidirectional guided resonances exploit complementary aspects of radiation, motivating a unified framework for controlling polarization and directionality together. Here we develop such a framework and introduce chiral unidirectional resonances (CURs) with arbitrarily high radiative quality factors and near-unity single-channel selectivity. We further extend this theory to guide the geometric design of arbitrary coherent emission states with prescribed radiative lifetimes. In addition, we establish scaling laws for the lifetime and radiation-state fidelity, and demonstrate robust chiral unidirectional emission over a finite momentum region. Our demonstrations provide a basis for single-sided circularly polarized light sources and polarization-matched optical coupling.

papers.title: Optimally Weighted Constrained Shadow Tomography for Reduced Density Matrices
papers.abstract: Accurate measurement of reduced density matrices (RDMs) is central to quantum simulations of many-fermion systems, but the required measurement resources remain a significant challenge. Constrained shadow tomography (CST) combines randomized measurements with $N$-representability conditions to reconstruct physically valid RDMs from limited measurement data. Here we improve CST by orthogonalizing the measurement constraints and using the resulting singular values to determine the relative weight of each independent measurement direction according to how strongly it is sampled by the quantum computer. These optimally weighted constraints are incorporated into the semidefinite program through a least-squares objective implemented with a Schur-complement relaxation. We demonstrate the approach for hydrogen chains on a quantum simulator and for azobenzene on a quantum processor. In both cases, optimally weighted CST systematically improves the accuracy of the reconstructed 2-RDM without increasing the measurement budget, providing a more measurement-efficient approach to partial tomography for quantum simulations of correlated fermions.

papers.title: Maximal input entropy for binary two-deletion and two-insertion channels
papers.abstract: Under uniform transmission, we determine the received binary words that maximize input entropy for two-deletion and two-insertion channels. For two deletions the maximizers are exactly the two alternating words at every positive received length. For two insertions the same conclusion holds from received length five onward; we give all smaller cases and exact maximal values. The proof combines an embedding-count identity organized by runs with strict convexity estimates, and a grouping of two-position deletion masks. For every insertion radius we give the complete positive embedding histogram of an alternating received word. We also determine its three-deletion histogram for every length, and certify all three-deletion maximizers through received length twelve and all three-insertion maximizers through length eighteen by exact integer comparison. These computations give precise three-error conjectures with their small-length exceptions.

papers.title: A characterization and closure property of Thorin's class
papers.abstract: Thorin's class coincides with the smallest class of probability laws on $\mathbb{R}$ that contains all gamma laws and their reflections, while being closed under convolution and weak convergence. In particular, all Thorin laws are self-decomposable. This paper proves an alternative characterization of Thorin's class in terms of what we call the hyperbolic Bochner-Bernstein property. This property corresponds to the notion of hyperbolically completely monotone Laplace transforms on the positive half line, but extended to the real-valued setting. Using the new characterization, it is shown that Thorin's class is closed under multiplication with independent random variables admitting hyperbolically completely monotone densities, which partly settles an open question raised by Bondesson and allows for proving that a large class of possibly skewed real-valued distributions is in Thorin's class. As particular examples, we apply the closure property to show that Johnson's S\textsubscript{U} distribution and the Pearson type IV distribution are in Thorin's class for all parameter choices.

papers.title: Quantitative Analytical Spheroid Model for Scattering-Type Scanning Near-Field Optical Spectroscopy of Layered Samples
papers.abstract: Scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) is a versatile tool for probing optical properties at deeply subwavelength scales. Its theoretical modeling, however, typically relies on computationally intensive numerical simulations or phenomenological analytical models, limiting quantitative spectral interpretation. In our previous work, we introduced an exact analytical solution for the quasi-electrostatic prolate spheroid model of s-SNOM for homogeneous bulk samples, combining the accuracy of numerical simulations with the efficiency of analytical approaches. Here, we generalize this framework to multilayer samples using two equivalent methods: a generalized image charge method and a Fourier integral method. The resulting exact spheroid model reproduces finite-element simulations within numerical precision while retaining the computational efficiency of an analytical model. We validate the model experimentally for poly (methyl methacrylate) layers of different thicknesses, showing that a single set of geometrical parameters simultaneously reproduces multiple demodulation harmonics and all measured thicknesses, unlike the finite dipole model. We further demonstrate its applicability to strongly resonant SiC layers on dielectric and photoexcited InAs substrates, where existing analytical approaches fail. The model provides an efficient quantitative framework for interpreting multilayer s-SNOM spectra and extracting local optical properties.

papers.title: Unlocking Low-Frequency Laser Doppler Holography Spectra for Functional Retinal and Choroidal Microvascular Phenotyping
papers.abstract: The low-frequency part of optical fluctuation spectra recorded by laser Doppler holography at a frame rate of 37~kHz is typically filtered out to reveal functional blood-flow waveforms in major retinal and choroidal vessels. We construct a time-varying spectral-excess (SE) distribution in capillary-associated territories by selecting complete cardiac cycles and applying successive spatial and beat medians in regions where vessels are unresolved and intermittent eye motion can dominate the signal. At each phase, spectral excess compares the integrated Doppler spectral area between two fixed low-frequency peaks near $\pm2$~kHz with a reference area defined by the high-frequency tail near $\pm18.5$~kHz. The resulting waveform, displayed against normalized cardiac phase, retains variation throughout the cardiac cycle and provides a basis for exploring its temporal organization. We summarize spectral-excess strength by the spectral excess index (SEI), defined as the temporal median of SE, and also describe an alternative evaluation after spectral pooling. A representative recording illustrates the construction. Physiological specificity and repeatability remain to be quantified.

papers.title: Two types of averaging principles for multiplicative stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equations with fast oscillations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study averaging principles for stochastic KdV equations perturbed by a fast oscillating term generated by a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, $ s\geq 0$. When dealing with multilinear estimates of the nonlinear terms in the stochastic KdV type equation, two kinds of workspace are both effective. The classical workspace can help us prove the averaging principle in the $L_ω^2$ sense, but it has more restrictions on the noise kernel and the conservation structures. When we use a new workspace without homogeneous low frequency restrictions, only the regularity conditions and the $L_x^2$ conservation structure is needed. Correspondingly, because there is no moment estimate of the solution, we can only prove the perturbed equations converge to an averaging equation in the probability sense. Our works may have important reference value, because it not only provides a new perspective to handle dynamical problems of stochastic dispersive model, but also compare it with the classical method.

papers.title: Self-Normalized Inference from Riemannian Stochastic Gradient Paths
papers.abstract: Riemannian stochastic gradient paths estimate constrained parameters, but confidence regions usually require estimating the Hessian and gradient-noise covariance. We develop self-normalized inference from one path by expressing retained iterates in a common random tangent space. Their average and centered partial sums share an unknown covariance factor that cancels in a Brownian bridge pivot. Under suitable regularity conditions, a joint expansion of the averaged estimator and integrated path controls nonlinear coordinate errors using conditional second moments. The procedure uses fixed-dimensional memory and extends to nondegenerate smooth functionals and alternative local coordinates. Numerical studies show competitive coverage relative to plug-in Wald inference while avoiding Hessian and residual-density estimation.

papers.title: Shared Randomness and Parallel Rounds in Permutation Sampling
papers.abstract: We study the shared randomness needed to sample a uniform permutation in parallel output rounds. Coordinates committed in the same round are independent conditional on the complete history and the current shared choice. Previous outputs are public; local computation and private randomness are free. We charge each shared choice by the logarithm of its conditional support size and sum these costs along the worst execution path. At every fixed round density $ρ\in(0,1)$, the optimal limiting total-variation error under any $o(n)$ shared budget matches the conditional-marginal optimum, even with arbitrary local kernels and adaptive coordination. A fixed improvement requires linear cost. For exact sampling in $R=Θ(n)$ rounds, the optimum is $nΦ(R/n)+O(\log n)$, where $Φ$ linearly interpolates $Φ(1/q)=\log q$. A protocol attaining this rate uses an initial seed and at most one further binary shared choice. When $\lceil n/2\rceil\le R\le n$, the finite optimum is $\log\binom{2(n-R)}{n-R}$, attained by an initial seed alone. The approximate converse uses an entropy inequality for sparse injections to control overlap with the target. The exact construction reuses randomness retained in a shared label partition after the first-stage outputs are exposed.

papers.title: Multiparameter quantum metrology for general and adaptive strategies
papers.abstract: We develop a conic-programming framework for multiparameter estimation of quantum processes under different classes of sensing strategies. Estimation precision depends on the choice of input probe state and measurement and, when a channel is used multiple times, on the arrangement of channel uses and intermediate controls. We specify different strategy classes through linear normalization constraints on generalized measurements, and formulate the local estimation problem using linear constraints and a linear objective function. We show that the separable-cone program gives the exact precision limit under the local estimation conditions considered here, while cone relaxations yield Cramér-Rao-type lower bounds. For $N$ uses of an identical quantum channel, we prove an exact $1/N$ scaling law for an RLD-based positive-cone lower bound, even for general process-matrix testers that allow indefinite causal order. Under the stated conditions on the channel and its parameter dependence, the minimum weighted mean-square error also scales as $1/N$. This extends an RLD-based restriction on Heisenberg scaling from adaptive strategies to this broader class. For fixed-order adaptive strategies, we show that each process-side conic bound equals the corresponding state-estimation bound optimized over sensor combs. We establish this equality by constructing a sensor comb from the process-side normalization operator. A noisy three-parameter field-sensing model illustrates the framework.

papers.title: Ground state and excitations of the \(C_2^{(1)}\) spin chain with non-diagonal boundaries
papers.abstract: Understanding boundary effects in higher-rank integrable quantum spin chains requires connecting exact spectral relations with the root configurations underlying their energies and excitations. With non-diagonal boundaries, determining these configurations remains challenging even when an exact spectral solution is available, hindering the direct extraction of thermodynamic properties. We address this problem for the rational $C_2^{(1)}$ chain by combining DMRG in the tensor-network framework with the quantum inverse scattering method. The numerically determined zeros of the fundamental and fused transfer-matrix eigenvalues reveal three bulk-string distributions, labeled by $x$, $y$, and $w$, together with boundary strings and additional roots. Substituting these configurations into the operator identities relating the two transfer matrices yields the ground-state energy and the surface energy in the thermodynamic limit under non-diagonal boundary conditions. The analytical surface energy agrees with the numerical results up to $O(\tfrac1N)$ corrections. From the regularity conditions of the operator identities, we derive a boundary-string selection rule and numerically identify allowed configurations beyond the ground state. For excitations preserving the boundary-string configuration, we identify three elementary hole excitations, $X$, $Y$, and $W$, in the $x$-, $y$-, and $w$-string distributions, respectively, and derive their energies. Based on the symmetry of the zero roots, we also present a bulk-excitation selection rule governing the allowed combinations of these elementary excitations in physical eigenstates. The framework developed here can therefore be used to systematically analyze boundary effects, bulk excitations, and related physical properties in other high-rank integrable quantum models with non-diagonal boundary conditions.

papers.title: Active Jarzynski and Crooks Relations for Driven Jump-Diffusions
papers.abstract: Non-conservative active driving breaks detailed balance in non-Gaussian jump-diffusions, obscuring the connection between external protocol work, housekeeping dissipation, and free-energy differences. Here, we establish exact finite-time fluctuation relations for driven Markov jump-diffusions---encompassing infinite-activity Lévy processes---by comparing path probabilities under the forward and current-reversed dual dynamics relative to the instantaneous steady state (ISS). We derive a trajectory-level decomposition of total entropy production that cleanly separates transient state relaxation, housekeeping heat, and external protocol driving. When the ISS takes a Gibbsian form, gauge-tilting the dual path measure yields an Active Jarzynski equality, $\langle\exp[-(W+Δs_{\mathrm{act}})]\rangle_{π_0}=e^{-ΔF}$, which incorporates active housekeeping entropy $Δs_{\mathrm{act}}$ alongside mechanical work $W$ and coexists with the conventional Jarzynski equality. Under protocol reversal, this dual framework further reveals an Active Crooks relation, where the asymmetry between forward and reverse work distributions is governed by the conditional exponential average of active dissipation. Our results provide a framework for recovering free-energy differences in driven jump-diffusions with Gibbsian instantaneous steady states and for characterizing active irreversibility through trajectory statistics.

papers.title: Excited-state-induced nonlinearity and polarity reversals in the thermocurrent through a quantum dot
papers.abstract: Quantum dots are electrically tuneable thermal machines capable of both energy harvesting and cooling at the nanoscale in the cryogenic regime. At large thermal biases, their thermoelectric transport shows a complex behaviour, including additional extrema and polarity reversals in the thermocurrent. Though these asymmetries and nonlinearities directly affect rectification and power conversion, their origin has not been studied systematically. We address this through measurements and modelling of a single GaAs/AlGaAs quantum dot whose source is heated by white-noise excitation. Using Pauli master equation for sequential tunnelling through a two-level dot, retaining the full Fermi distributions of both leads, distinct tunnel rates for the two levels, and relaxation between them, we show that the excited state acts as a second transport channel which competes with the ground-state contribution. Strong excited-state coupling combined with slow relaxation produces polarity reversals in the thermocurrent; without both, the excited state yields only additional extrema and an amplitude asymmetry across the charge degeneracy point. Experimentally, as the source temperature increases, an additional extremum emerges in the thermocurrent which develops into a polarity reversal. Using the excited-state level spacing and ground-state tunnel rate obtained independently from pulsed-gate and bias spectroscopies, the model reproduces the positions of the observed extrema and their amplitudes to within a factor of about three, placing the device in the regime of slow relaxation and strong excited-state coupling. Our results establish thermocurrent line-shape as a probe of excited-state tunnelling and relaxation in quantum dots. Excited states, often treated as a minor correction, can dominate quantum-dot thermoelectric transport far from equilibrium.

papers.title: Source shapes in coordinate and momentum space in $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}$ = 200 GeV Au+Au collisions
papers.abstract: In high-energy heavy-ion physics, femtoscopy aims to explore and understand the space-time characteristics of the collisions through investigating the correlation function of particle pairs. In recent years, experimental measurements have shown that the shape of the particle source function can be well described by the Lévy distribution, motivating further phenomenological studies. In this work, we perform a three-dimensional analysis of the source shapes for different particle-pair types in $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}=200$ GeV Au+Au collisions generated with the EPOS event generator. In contrast to our previous analyses, where we fitted the one-dimensional projections of the pair distribution function, $D(ρ_j)$ ($j \in \{\text{out}, \text{side}, \text{long}\}$), now we reconstruct the three-dimensional $C(\boldsymbol{q})$ correlation function and fit it directly, as in experimental analyses. Furthermore, we now apply full three-dimensional fits instead of fitting the one-dimensional projections. We find that this approach results in smaller Lévy index values, while the direction averaged Lévy scale and the correlation strength remain largely unchanged, except for kaons. In the case of pions, the $α$ values are closer to the PHENIX data, showing a good agreement above 20\% centrality.

papers.title: Melting noncoplanar order on the square-kagome lattice: Chiral, flat-band, and staggered spin liquids from projective symmetry
papers.abstract: Noncoplanar magnetic orders carry a scalar spin chirality, and their melting by quantum fluctuations has been proposed as a route to chiral spin liquids. We ask what this route can produce on the square-kagome lattice, where couplings across the octagons stabilize noncoplanar cuboc and conical orders. We classify the fermionic spin liquids of this lattice by their projective symmetry groups, identify the symmetry class into which each noncoplanar order would melt, and compare candidate states with Gutzwiller-projected wave functions. A magnetic selection rule constrains the route: the chirality of every cuboc and conical order alternates in space, so a liquid that keeps the symmetry of its parent order has zero Chern number and no spontaneous thermal Hall response. A Chern state can descend only from uniformly chiral orders, and the regular ones we find need ferromagnetic bow-tie couplings. The energetics do not favor a chiral liquid either: among the projected wave functions we compare, a cuboc1-ordered state is lowest for strong cross-octagon couplings, and nonchiral states, a valence-bond crystal or a time-reversal-symmetric liquid, for weaker ones. The two inequivalent site orbits shape the spinons: a relative time-reversal sign between them pins flat bands to the Fermi level, and because the translations of $p4mm$ are not commutators, staggered chiral liquids exist, which are absent on sixfold-symmetric lattices.

papers.title: HALO: Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records
papers.abstract: Learning from extensive longitudinal clinical records--spanning repeated encounters, evolving conditions, and heterogeneous documentation--under a finite labeling budget requires solving two coupled problems: deciding what evidence to keep and deciding which patients deserve higher-fidelity labels. Prior work on active learning and multi-fidelity label acquisition mainly addresses the second problem, while treating the evidence presented to the acquisition policy as fixed. We present HALO, a Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning pipeline for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records. This framework jointly learns what to read and what label source to acquire under budget. HALO first selects informative evidence from longitudinal records and then uses a budget-aware policy to allocate free-, silver-, and gold-fidelity label sources. For frozen policies, our theory characterizes asymmetric acquired-label channels and gives a budget-constrained finite-sample gold-risk bound for a common downstream logistic model. In a heart-failure case study, HALO attained the highest MedAlign acquired-label F1 at six of eight target budgets. A downstream classifier trained on HALO-acquired labels attained the highest external MGB F1 at budgets 15-60 and remained within 0.01 of the best comparator at budgets 75-120.

papers.title: Normal Factor Graph Representations of Stabilizer Quantum Codes with Applications
papers.abstract: We develop normal factor graph (NFG) representations of stabilizer quantum error-correcting codes and entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes. We introduce two complementary representations. Quantum-code NFGs describe stabilizer and normalizer label codes and provide a graphical framework for establishing self-orthogonality, constructing codes from component codes, and identifying encoding and decoding circuits. Quantum-probability NFGs represent the quantum-mechanical probabilities associated with encoding, noise, and measurement. We also introduce a doubleedge formulation that makes the relationship between these two representations explicit. We apply the framework to convolutional and tail-biting convolutional stabilizer codes, as well as to two classes of low-density parity-check stabilizer codes. Finally, we extend the quantum-probability representation to entanglementassisted codes.

papers.title: Invariant universal averages and Bertrand's paradox: a response to Shackel
papers.abstract: In 2014, with D. Aerts we proposed a solution to the hard problem of Bertrand's paradox by means of a universal average over different ways of randomizing an entity. In his recent monograph, N. Shackel raises objections concerning the approximation by cellular densities, the restrictions used in their construction, the apparently trivial limit of their averages, the choice of a second-order probability law, and the dependence of the result on the naming of chords. We revisit these objections using the invariance-based formulation of the universal average. The first objection is well taken, and the approximation argument is repaired: an explicit sequence of bivalent cellular densities provides weak approximation of any prescribed probability measure, with an error bound for intervals. We show that any second-order selection law invariant under rearrangements of equal-length cells has the same uniform barycenter, independently of the particular densities and weights employed. For cellular densities, this conclusion holds exactly at every finite resolution. Thus, non-uniqueness of the second-order law does not prevent uniqueness of the resulting average within the indifferent class. Finally, we prove that no probability measure can be invariant under both these rearrangements and arbitrary changes of interval lengths. The reference geometry therefore cannot be obtained by averaging alone: it must be supplied by the physical modelization of the randomized entity. These results clarify the scope, and the limitations, of our original distinction between the easy and hard problems of Bertrand's paradox.

papers.title: Optimal Learning in Fairness-Aware Contextual Bandits
papers.abstract: Mitigating unfair disparities in sequential decision-making is a growing concern in machine learning. We study contextual bandits under a global covariate-based Lipschitz fairness constraint, pioneered by \cite{dwork2012fairness}, requiring individuals with similar contexts to receive similar action distributions. We show that this constraint induces a randomisation region near the decision boundary and explicitly quantify the population level cost of fairness. We further establish a canonical representation of the optimal fair policy, which reduces the fair policy design to a lower-dimensional boundary optimisation problem. We develop a lazy fair greedy algorithm that exploits fairness-induced covariate diversity under continuous contexts, with policy updates computed via finite-dimensional linear programming. For general context distributions, including discrete and mixed contexts, we propose a lazy polyhedral upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm, whose optimistic optimisation reduces to finitely many linear programs over confidence-set vertices. Both methods satisfy fairness at every round and achieve regret of order $O(\sqrt{T} + T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}{\indc\{d\geq 4\}})$ up to poly-logarithmic factors, where $d$ is the dimension of the contexts. A matching minimax lower bound for $\ell_1$-based fairness establishes optimality, and reveals an unavoidable nonparametric cost of learning the decision boundary, which dominates the parametric learning cost when $d \geq 4$. Experiments on synthetic and real data support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.

papers.title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
papers.abstract: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $μ_n \to μ$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.

papers.title: Spontaneous Chirality and Collective Chern Bands in a Dipole-Conserving Bose System
papers.abstract: We demonstrate spontaneous chiral dipole order and an isolated collective Chern band in a time-reversal-symmetric microscopic bosonic lattice model with exact dipole-moment conservation. In a controlled large-occupation limit at zero temperature, frustrated dipole exchange and three-particle conversion stabilize two time-reversed chiral condensates. The two dipole Goldstone modes remain gapless, while a separate finite-frequency band carries Chern numbers $-1$ and $+1$ in the opposite domains. We trace this topology to complex mode couplings in the chiral background that gap finite-frequency Dirac crossings. Site-resolved density drives preserve dipole-moment conservation and reconstruct the band Chern number from band-resolved absorption spectra in the quadratic theory.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of heavy quarkonia and their nonrelativistic expansion in a self-consistent light-front quark model
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational form factors of the pseudoscalar heavy quarkonia $η_c(1S,2S)$ and $η_b(1S,2S)$ in a light-front quark model with physical radial wave functions represented by orthogonal mixtures of the two lowest harmonic-oscillator basis states $φ_{1S}$ and $φ_{2S}$. The Bakamjian--Thomas prescription is applied consistently to constituent matrix elements and Lorentz prefactors at the integrand level. Working in the $Δ^+=0$ frame with $Δ=P'-P$ and $t=Δ^2$, we extract $A_q(t)$ from the quark energy--momentum tensor components $T_q^{++}$, $T_q^{+i}$, and $T_q^{ij}$, and $D_q(t)$ from $T_q^{+-}$, $T_q^{-i}$, and $T_q^{ii}$ using appropriate momentum-transfer projections. The independent extractions agree in the full relativistic calculation and in the analytic nonrelativistic expansions through $ O(v^2)$, where $v=β/m_Q$, $β$ is the Gaussian width, and $m_Q$ is the constituent mass. At zero momentum transfer, the expansions give $D_q^{φ_{1S}}(0)=-v^2+ O(v^4)$ and $D_q^{φ_{2S}}(0)=-2/3-(13/3)v^2+O(v^4)$. The interference, defined as the sum of the two cross overlaps, first contributes as $D_q^{\mathrm{cross}}(0)=-(4/\sqrt{6})v^2+O(v^4)$. Thus, the pure Gaussian $1S$ contribution is suppressed, whereas a nonzero $2S$ admixture at fixed mixing angle leaves an $O(v^0)$ D-term in the physical ground state. Full numerical results for the mixed states illustrate the effects of heavy-quark flavor and radial structure on mass distributions and internal stresses.

papers.title: Riemannian Newton Methods with Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: We develop online statistical inference for Polyak-Ruppert averages of inexact Newton iterates on Riemannian manifolds. A local asymptotic representation separates observation noise, solver randomization, and accumulated implementation bias, and yields one-pass covariance estimators and asymptotically valid Wald regions under local regularity and centering conditions. Independent fresh solves add a positive semidefinite term to the score-sandwich covariance; averaging solver replicas reduces this term in inverse proportion to their number. Slowly varying predictable gains instead cancel from the first order law. Product torus simulations show how Newton scaling shortens an ill-conditioned transient and how retaining solver variation restores coverage. Intrinsic means and principal subspaces provide geometric applications, with a streaming data illustration.

papers.title: Bootstrap Inference for Riemannian Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: We develop an online multiplier bootstrap for manifold-valued parameters estimated by averaging the iterates of Riemannian stochastic approximation. The method runs weighted iterations alongside the original algorithm, with each path using the same observations while updating its own state and intrinsic average. The weighted averages provide uncertainty assessments without a plug-in asymptotic covariance estimator. Under local stability and regularity conditions, we establish bootstrap consistency and show that a fixed number of paths suffices for asymptotically valid Student intervals and intrinsic confidence regions. The theory accommodates samplewise nonsmooth scores and identifies a critical oracle-bias regime in which the estimator's limiting distribution shifts, but the centered bootstrap distribution does not. Applications include spherical means, positive-definite matrix means and medians, and principal-subspace estimation. Simulations show coverage close to nominal in regular settings, and an analysis of North Atlantic storm locations illustrates descriptive online inference for a spherical center.

papers.title: Single-Mode Squeezing Using Degenerate Four-Wave Mixing in a Dual-Pump TWPA
papers.abstract: Single-mode squeezing of the electromagnetic vacuum is a key resource for mode-selective noise reduction in quantum measurements. At microwave frequencies, single-mode squeezing is typically obtained by using Josephson and Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers designed for three-wave mixing operation. In single-pump degenerate four-wave mixing, the coincidence of pump, signal, and idler frequencies complicates separation of the squeezed field from the strong pump. A dual-pump configuration enables degenerate operation while keeping both pumps spectrally separated from the squeezed mode. Here, we demonstrate single-mode squeezing in a flux-tunable, dual-pump Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier, employing reversed-Kerr phase matching. By independently calibrating the single-pump gains, we find that the strongest squeezing occurs along approximately balanced-gain trajectories, while the optimal squeezing does not necessarily correspond to the highest dual-pump gain. At flux biases $Φ_\mathrm{ext}/Φ_0 = 0.0$ and $0.5$, the minimum quadrature noise levels reach $-2.48 \pm 0.18~\mathrm{dB}$ and $-1.62 \pm 0.20~\mathrm{dB}$ relative to vacuum, respectively. These results establish the proposed architecture as a platform for single-mode squeezing in microwave continuous-variable quantum technologies.

papers.title: A dual approach to $L^p$ estimates for orthogonal martingales satisfying the differential subordination
papers.abstract: We develop a new dual approach, which can be used to establish sharp $L^p$ bounds for orthogonal differentially subordinate martingales. The method rests on the construction of a certain special function enjoying appropriate majorization properties and a novel differential condition.

papers.title: Binary Quantum Hypothesis Testing with a Rejection Option: The Exact Error-Exponent Trade-off
papers.abstract: We characterize the exact error-exponent trade-off in binary quantum hypothesis testing with a rejection option for faithful states on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. The probabilities of rejection under the two hypotheses are required to vanish exponentially, with exponents at least $K$ and $L$. We show that a quadruple $(a,b,K,L)$ of positive error and rejection exponents is achievable if and only if it satisfies three single-letter conditions: two conditions involve Petz--Rényi quantities and coincide with the converse bound conjectured to be tight by Ji and Regula; the third involves the $α$--$z$ Rényi quantities on the triangle $\max\{α,1-α\}\le z\le1$. The proof combines a sector decomposition inside Schur--Weyl blocks, an explicit one-shot measurement construction, and an exact minimax argument.

papers.title: From Kination to Detection: Scotogenic Scalar Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar dark matter in the scotogenic model during an early kination-dominated epoch. The enhanced expansion rate causes earlier freeze-out and increases the relic abundance, opening viable dark matter masses from approximately $200~\mathrm{GeV}$ to $1~\mathrm{TeV}$ while reducing the need for co-annihilation with a nearly degenerate singlet fermion. Current indirect searches strongly constrain the $(100-200)~\mathrm{GeV}$ region, whereas much of the surviving parameter space can be probed by CTA and next-generation direct detection experiments. The viable spectra also lead to complementary collider signatures, including missing transverse energy, displaced leptons, and disappearing charged tracks, providing promising tests at the HL-LHC and future lepton colliders.

papers.title: Latin cubes of order $4$ and $4320$-point quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$
papers.abstract: Possibly the most enduring lower-bound record for kissing numbers in dimensions greater than $8$ (excluding $24$) is $$ κ_{16}\geq 4320. $$ This lower bound is attained by a shell of the famous Barnes--Wall lattice, which was discovered in 1959. Besides this configuration, at least one alternative $4320$-point kissing arrangement is currently known. Recently, it was noticed that all these configurations can be described in terms of the so-called quaternionic construction, a general type of construction that was instrumental in explaining the geometry of the $841$-point kissing arrangement in ${\mathbb R}^{12}$. We give a simple generalization of quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$ obtained from record configurations. They are parameterized by three Latin cubes of order $4$, six permutations of $3$-element set, and are all infinitesimally jammed. Computer-aided counting shows that there are $4\,072\,728\,621$ isometry classes in this family of $4320$-point kissing arrangements.

papers.title: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes
papers.abstract: We prove a fixed-characteristic density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes: for each prime $p$, the lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic $p$ have natural density zero. Thus, for almost every length coprime to $p$, every such code over every finite field of characteristic $p$ has only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof uses the Feng--Hollmann--Li--Xiang classification for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions in that paper, and a theorem by Wiertelak on multiplicative orders, in the form recalled by Moree.

papers.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
papers.abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form. On each simplex, we replace the uniform probability density function (PDF) with a Gaussian PDF that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, arriving at the information projection onto the family of Gaussian PDFs. By exploiting affine isomorphisms between simplices, the joint convexity and bijection invariance properties of the KL divergence, identities for Dirichlet PDFs, and a partition-of-unity argument, we establish a dimension-dependent but geometry-independent sharp upper bound on the global KL divergence between the resulting GM PDF and the uniform PDF on the original domain. Numerical examples illustrate the construction and demonstrate its potential in practical applications.

papers.title: Sensitivity of the IceCube atmospheric muon rate to decadal trends in the effective atmospheric temperature
papers.abstract: Decadal changes in the Antarctic stratosphere, generally associated with ozone recovery and shifts in polar circulation, are of broad geophysical interest. However, independent long-term measurements of the atmosphere above the Antarctic interior are scarce. We assess whether the atmospheric muon rate recorded by IceCube could constrain decadal changes in the effective atmospheric temperature, $T_\mathrm{eff}$, a weighted average of temperature through the atmosphere that is most sensitive to the stratosphere. Using public atmospheric reanalysis data and records of cosmic-ray, solar, and geomagnetic variability, we reproduce the measured seasonal response of the IceCube muon rate. We then test whether the same response applies to long-term temperature changes with a different vertical temperature profile. The limiting requirement is detector stability rather than counting statistics: an unmodeled muon rate drift of $1\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$ would mimic a temperature trend of $2.8\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. The long-term rate must therefore be stable to approximately $0.3\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$. Within this budget, snow accumulation contributions can be constrained. For a 14-year record, atmospheric variability gives a one-sided 95% CL statistical sensitivity of $1.6\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. Given this sensitivity, the $\sim0.9\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$ cooling indicated by the 2011-2025 atmospheric records would become distinguishable after approximately 30 years of measurement.

papers.title: Quantum Mpemba effect of Z2 symmetry restoration in the Dicke model
papers.abstract: We study a symmetry-restoration quantum Mpemba effect in the dissipative Dicke model as an example of a weakly $\mathbb Z_2$-symmetric open quantum system, where the full Liouvillian is parity covariant although individual quantum jumps connect the two Hilbert-space parity sectors. Using the entanglement-asymmetry (EA) diagnostic to monitor parity restoration, we compare coherent-product and cat-product initial states. Coherent-product states show conventional relaxation, with larger initial asymmetry decaying more slowly and no Mpemba crossing observed. Cat-product states, by contrast, can reverse this hierarchy over a finite region of initial-state space. This reversal is enabled by initial-state mode filtering: the cat-product superposition suppresses the contributions of the leading slow Liouvillian modes, allowing a more asymmetric state to restore parity through faster decay channels. Our results reveal that symmetry-restoration QME can arise even when parity is preserved only as a weak Liouvillian symmetry, with quantum jumps mixing the Hilbert-space parity sectors. The anomalous relaxation is governed by initial-state-dependent filtering of the leading slow Liouvillian modes, providing a mechanism for symmetry-restoration QME beyond strongly conserved symmetry sectors.

papers.title: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242
papers.abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242. Equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of a Boolean function in nine variables is 242. Our proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with a spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities. We first show that every nine-variable Boolean function of nonlinearity 243 admits a unique one-point modification that raises its nonlinearity to 244: the point to be changed is the vector sum of its support. This part uses exact Walsh-update identities, integer interpolation, rigidity of a quadratic residue, and a sharp Walsh l1 estimate for cubic Boolean functions. To exclude nonlinearity 244, we use Parseval's identity and congruences of integral Walsh coefficients to force an exceptionally restricted spectrum. An associated cubic residue phase must attain the extremal Walsh l1 bound 10240. We eliminate one equality spectrum by hyperplane slicing; the other forces the original Boolean function from the signs of the cubic phase and yields a double-complement-pairing identity for its cubic top part. The classification of alternating trilinear forms over F2, an exact filter of their representatives, and two exhaustive enumerations of 218 quadratic supplements then rule out every remaining candidate. Together with the known construction attaining nonlinearity 242, these arguments establish the asserted covering radius.

papers.title: Where Does a Variational Quantum Classifier Lose Accuracy? Angle Encoding, Readout and the Fidelity-Kernel Reference in Cyberattack Detection
papers.abstract: When a variational quantum classifier performs poorly at detecting network attacks, it is hard to tell which part is to blame: the encoding, the trained circuit or the readout, which turns measurements into a class. In this work, we build upon a recent amplitude-encoded classifier, and we try to separate their contributions to the NSL-KDD benchmark in noiseless simulation. We compare angle and amplitude encoding, vary one component at a time, and measure each circuit against a classical yardstick: a support-vector machine on the encoded states, whose accuracy estimates what a well-trained circuit can reach. Most of the shortfall lies in the readout. Reading one qubit, or the parity of all qubits, leaves several percentage points unused, while a readout trained together with the circuit recovers most of them from the same measurements. This also explains why some classifiers stop improving as further layers are added. The encodings suit different needs. Angle encoding gives the more accurate detector on traffic like the training data and, from eight features up, shallower circuits; amplitude encoding needs far fewer qubits and catches more attacks of types never seen in training. Finally, we report that classical models, given the same inputs, are about as accurate as the best circuits, thus, registering no quantum advantage.

papers.title: Experimental Realization of a Nonreciprocal Quantum Battery
papers.abstract: Quantum batteries promise faster and more efficient energy storage and extraction by harnessing quantum mechanics, serving as essential building blocks for future quantum devices. A key practical requirement-unidirectional energy flow during charging-is straightforward in classical batteries via potential difference, yet remains a major challenge in the quantum regime due to the inherent reciprocity of coherent coupling. Here, we realize the first backflow-free, nonreciprocal quantum battery in the few-quantum regime, implemented in a highly controlled trapped-ion system via a qubit-reservoir engineering technique. By subtly tailoring quantum interference between coherent and dissipative couplings of two laser-cooled motional modes, we achieve strictly unidirectional energy flow from the charger to the battery. We observe maximum charging power at an exceptional point and demonstrate a complete charge-discharge cycle with unitary work extraction. This work establishes the foundation for directional energy transfer and storage in micro- and nanoscale quantum devices, with broad implications for nonreciprocal energy harvesting, precision metrology, information processing, and quantum thermodynamics.

papers.title: Multicopy teleportation and quantum program retrieval on superconducting quantum hardware
papers.abstract: Correction-free teleportation protocols offer a probabilistic route around the limits imposed by the quantum no-programming theorem, but have remained largely theoretical. Here, we experimentally implement and benchmark correction-free multicopy teleportation on noisy superconducting quantum hardware. Key to this is an efficient circuit implementation: by suitably decomposing the unitary that maps the multicopy measurement basis onto the computational basis, we substantially reduce circuit depth and gate count. For one- and two-qubit input states, using $k=2$ and $3$ copies, we observe success probabilities substantially exceeding the single-copy bound with fidelities above 0.85. We further explore applications to probabilistic programmable quantum processors, in particular the storage and retrieval of unitary operations encoded in quantum program states. Our results establish the practical feasibility of multicopy teleportation and highlight its potential for near-term quantum processors and distributed quantum computing.

papers.title: How tightly can PBH abundance information constrain scalar-induced gravitational waves?
papers.abstract: Primordial black hole (PBH) abundances and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) probe the same primordial fluctuations through different physical weights. We examine the predictive power of precise synthetic information on absolute PBH abundances over a finite stellar-mass interval, together with an exact total abundance and external population bounds. For Gaussian perturbations under a fixed quantum chromodynamics (QCD) formation prescription, two smooth, symmetric lognormal spectra satisfy the same abundance conditions while producing nonproportional leading-order SIGW spectra. The two spectra differ by about 20% when averaged over the lower of two adjacent nanohertz windows but by nearly a factor of 60 in the higher-frequency window, so the difference cannot be represented by a single rescaling of the gravitational-wave background. Peak position and width compensate with amplitude in the abundance calculation, while the higher-frequency window draws almost all its energy from scalar-mode pairs with both wavenumbers above the primordial peak. Under the principal abundance benchmark, local finite-width components yield larger contrasts at a fixed nanohertz frequency through distinct mode couplings under both the QCD and stochastic peak-curvature formation prescriptions. For a separately generated population, extending mass information over most of its abundance restricts the lognormal peak-position and width compensation and reduces the higher-window contrast, while the unequal window responses persist. These results show why joint PBH-SIGW inference must propagate primordial shapes compatible with the PBH abundance information rather than assign one tensor template to a single abundance fit.

papers.title: Noise Stability on the Hypercube: Order $7/8$
papers.abstract: For a balanced Boolean function $f$ on the discrete hypercube, we study the $α$-stability $\mathbb{E}[(T_ρf)^α]$, where $T_ρ$ is the Boolean noise operator and $0<α<1$. Using the asymmetric Hellinger kernel estimates recently established by OpenAI, we prove that dictators minimize the $7/8$-stability in every dimension and at every correlation $0\leρ\le1$. At interior correlations they are the only minimizers. As a consequence, dictators minimize the $α$-stability for every $7/8\leα<1$, maximize the $α$-stability for every $1<α<2$, and maximize the one-sided Shannon entropy stability $\mathbb{E}[T_ρf\log T_ρf]$. This resolves a conjecture of Li and Médard and strengthens the Courtade--Kumar conjecture in the balanced setting.

papers.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
papers.abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.

papers.title: Excess inner-horizon entropy and the thermodynamics of Kerr formation
papers.abstract: \noindent We develop a charge-matched thermodynamic framework for the regular rotating black-hole family underlying an exact model of Kerr formation. Since the Kerr endpoint already possesses a Cauchy horizon, hidden entropy is identified with the excess inner-horizon area relative to Kerr at fixed mass $M$ and angular momentum $J=Ma$: $\Sexc=π[h_c^2-(r_-^{\Kerr})^2]$, where $h_c$ is the regular inner-horizon radius and $r_-^{\Kerr}=M-\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$. Under regularity and interior-profile assumptions, we prove $r_-^{\Kerr}<h_c<h$ and establish the sharp bound $0<\Sexc<4πM\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$. The Schwarzschild limit yields $\Sexc=πh_c^2$, while $\Sexc=0$ at the Kerr endpoint. The Kerr reference entropy satisfies $S_+^{\Kerr}+S_-^{\Kerr}=4πM^2$, so rotation redistributes its two-horizon contributions at fixed mass. For the time-dependent model, we derive exact evolution equations for the inner root and $\Sexc$, interpreted as root-bookkeeping identities unless the roots are established as dynamical horizons. In the minimal $N=1$ trajectory, the apparent pole at $n=2$ is removable in the mass profile, giving a logarithmic continuation of the root equation, although the stationary curvature is singular there. The stationary Ricci-scalar density is locally absolutely integrable for $-1<n\leq2$, with the Kerr endpoint $n=-1$ treated separately. Minkowski breaking occurs at $n=0$, independently of inner-horizon disappearance. Quasi-extremal regular configurations approach, but cannot attain, the entropy bound without losing a regular Killing horizon.

papers.title: Low-PAPR Rank-2 DFT-s-OFDM Waveform for 6G Uplink
papers.abstract: Rank-2 discrete Fourier transform-spread orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DFT-s-OFDM) is attracting renewed interest for 6G uplink, offering not only spatial multiplexing gains but also an additional degree of freedom for peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction. We exploit this freedom by selectively exchanging constellation symbols between the two layers before DFT spreading, preserving the transmitted information while reshaping the resulting waveforms. Building on this idea, we propose Cyclic Layer Assignment with Shared-basis Synthesis (CLASS). CLASS employs carefully designed cyclic assignment patterns to generate diverse waveform candidates, while reusing a small number of waveform components to avoid synthesizing each candidate separately. We further establish the optimality of the cyclic design in maximizing waveform diversity under a minimum-basis constraint when equal group sizes are feasible. With only six inverse DFTs, CLASS explores 16 assignments and reduces the 99th-percentile worst-layer PAPR by 1.41 dB relative to fixed assignment, outperforming representative selected mapping (SLM) and partial transmit sequences (PTS) schemes under the same synthesis budget.

papers.title: High-order concentric hopfions in a helimagnet
papers.abstract: Magnetic hopfions are three-dimensional topological solitons: ``knots'' in the vector field of magnetization of magnetically ordered materials, which are a key element of the three-dimensional spintronics emerging today. In this work, a simple analytical model for a new type of magnetic hopfions --- ``concentric'' ones --- is constructed and solved. Their size and equilibrium energy are estimated, their stability region on the magnetic phase diagram of a helimagnet is mapped out, and the requirements for materials admitting equilibrium concentric hopfions with high Hopf index on a uniformly magnetized background are determined.

papers.title: The Self-repelling Burglar
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the conditional location of $X_T$ given the local time profile $L_T(\cdot)$ for two non-Markovian self-interacting processes: the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM) and the true self-repelling motion (TSRM). For TSRM, our novel approach yields a new proof of Dumaz's clever burglar result [Dumaz 2012].

papers.title: What Is the Dynamic Capacitance of a Memristor?
papers.abstract: Impedance spectroscopy of memristors, nanofluidic channels and halide perovskite devices often shows a low-frequency capacitance that is orders of magnitude larger than any plausible stored charge, or that becomes negative and appears together with an inductive loop. We distinguish two kinds of capacitance that enter the impedance in the same way: a storage capacitance, the derivative of a stored charge, and a dynamic capacitance, produced by the delayed response of a conduction current. Using the conductance-activated quasi-linear memristor (CALM) model, and a general memristor in which an internal state controls the conductance, we show that the dynamic capacitance is the time integral of the transient differential conductance after a small voltage step, measured from its final value. For a single relaxing state it is the product of a relaxing conductance and a relaxation time, with a negative sign. It vanishes at zero bias, and its sign is set by whether the stationary conductance increases or decreases with the magnitude of the voltage. Potentiation gives a negative capacitance and a chemical inductor, and depression gives a positive capacitance that is easily mistaken for stored charge. The analysis gives an explicit formulation of the time-domain criterion for negative capacitance of Jonscher and Ershov. In conical multipore nanofluidic membranes, the dynamic capacitance obtained from impedance and from voltage pulses shows the same sign change at zero bias and reaches values several hundred times larger than the membrane capacitance. The same picture accounts for the capacitive and inductive regimes of halide perovskite memristors.
