We consider here the use of a broader class of boundaries, called elastic, which involves one free parameter interpolating between these two limiting cases. We show how the conventional stochastic-$δN$, and its recently proposed time-reversed counterpart adapt to such a class of boundary behaviour. As an illustration, we solve time-reversed stochastic inflation for an exactly flat semi-infinite potential with an elastic boundary, a setup where the standard stochastic-$δN$ formalism breaks down, and compare the results to the purely absorbing case. Quantitative differences are found in terms of skewness and tail behaviour. This suggests that the transition between stochastic inflation and subsequent evolution may have observable consequences. Finally, we show that an elastic boundary stands as an effective model for stochastic tunnelling through a Dirac delta potential barrier. This mechanism can be equivalently framed as a smooth transition of stochastic trajectories in a mirror virtual medium with specific absorption properties.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic second-order oracle complexity of solving smooth convex finite-sum optimization with $n$ components. Very recently, Tsedenov \& Kovalev (2026) showed that the minimax optimal complexity under averaged smoothness and convexity is $\tildeΘ(n + n^{6/7} ε^{-2/7})$ by establishing nearly matching upper and lower bounds. In this paper, we show that individual smoothness and convexity provably enable further acceleration, where the lower complexity bound is $Ω(n+ n^{5/7} ε^{-2/7})$ under this stronger assumption. Then, by establishing a novel second-order self-bounding inequality, we design a new Taylor-corrected lazy Newton method, which can lead to a better complexity of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n + n^{5/7} ε^{-2/7})$ by applying the optimal Monteiro-Svaiter acceleration, matching our lower bound up to only logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Determining the meson spectrum directly from Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) remains a central challenge, since QCD is strongly coupled at low energies and most excited states appear as resonances in hadronic decay channels. Advances in lattice QCD and scattering theory now provide a systematic framework for extracting meson spectra and resonance properties from first principles. Here I present an overview of this program and review current state-of-the-art calculations in meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD. I highlight recent progress in the extraction of resonant and coupled-channel amplitudes, along with frontier developments in three-body dynamics and the determination of meson photo-couplings. Together, these advances are bringing us closer to a comprehensive first-principles description of the excited meson spectrum.

papers.title: The Devil Went Down to de Sitter: Divergent Effective Field Theory Expansions in Cosmology
papers.abstract: Effective field theories (EFTs) in de Sitter space, and in accelerating cosmologies more generally, must capture phenomena absent in flat space, most notably long-range correlations generated by spontaneous particle production. When heavy physics is integrated out in such time-dependent backgrounds, these effects leave an imprint on the EFT expansion: even at tree level, this is generically an asymptotic rather than convergent series. This is not a failure of EFT. The large-order behavior of the expansion coefficients encodes physical information inaccessible at any finite order, so cosmological EFTs contain hidden data. Using resurgence analysis, we show how this information can be systematically extracted to recover exact and non-perturbative predictions from the perturbative expansion. In the example we study, the resurgent completion is naturally organized in terms of the de Sitter $S$-matrix. This leads us to conjecture a prescription for extracting $S$-matrix data from cosmological EFTs in general. The framework extends to any setting where particle production, or a similar non-perturbative phenomenon, renders the EFT expansion asymptotic. A longer companion paper will provide a more detailed and pedagogical treatment.

papers.title: Capacity Meets the Four Subspace Problem: Distributed Linear Computation and the Cross-Ratio
papers.abstract: $K$ users each observe a fixed linear function of common data over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and a server must recover another fixed linear function with zero error from one message sent by each user. The capacity, the minimum total number of symbols the users send per computed instance, depends only on the configuration of subspaces formed by these linear functions. We study the instance in which three users observe $\boldsymbol{a}$, $\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{a}+\boldsymbol{b}$ and the server wants $\boldsymbol{a}+λ\boldsymbol{b}$. The four functions span four lines in a plane with cross-ratio $λ$, the smallest instance of the four subspace problem of representation theory. It is the smallest configuration whose capacity is not determined by the dimensions of the subspaces formed by sums and intersections: these dimensions are the same for every $λ$, but the capacity depends on the cross-ratio and on the prime subfield. For the harmonic cross-ratios, $λ=-1$, $λ=2$ or $2λ=1$, it is $2$: every zero-error code reveals $(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b})$ to the server, so no code beats having two users send their observations. For $λ$ outside the prime subfield it is the cut-set bound $3/2$, achieved by codes linear over the prime subfield, while codes linear over the field need $2$. For the other $λ$ in the prime subfield it lies in $[3p/(2p-1),2]$, so no code at any block length approaches the cut-set bound. The qualitative separation persists under vanishing error for uniform data: the cut-set bound is tight exactly for $λ$ outside the prime subfield. The four-line instance is also exact repair of one node of a $[4,2]$ MDS storage code, and the results translate to that setting.

papers.title: Bootstrapping a Higher-Derivative Cosmological Collider: Borel-Laplace Resummation and Stokes Phenomena
papers.abstract: We develop a higher-derivative cosmological bootstrap for massive spectators with quartic dispersion, $ω^2\propto k^4$, revealing a new boundary-value problem for inflationary correlators. The exchange equation becomes fourth order, and the collapsed limit becomes an irregular singular point, where collider and WKB branches coexist and exhibit Stokes phenomena. Since the folded configuration is now an ordinary point, the relativistic criterion of Bunch--Davies regularity at the folded singularity is no longer available. We instead impose an asymptotic boundary condition that removes the WKB branches and matches the surviving collider branches to Schwinger-Keldysh data. We also construct a convergent Borel-Laplace particular solution that resums a factorially divergent expansion and satisfies both bootstrap equations simultaneously; its leading collapsed-limit behavior is reproduced by direct in-in integrals. In the bispectrum, the squeezed-limit collider signal retains its mass-dependent frequency, while its amplitude and phase depend on the dispersion scale; near the equilateral configuration, the full shape is also sensitive to this scale and can change sign. Our results expose a new analytic structure of non-relativistic cosmological correlators and signatures beyond the squeezed limit.

papers.title: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a finite spanning multiset of points in ${\rm PG}(k-1,q)$, and let ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ be its character function. For $1\le r\le k$, we study the maximum number of distinct values attained by ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ on the codimension-$r$ flats under a total-multiplicity budget. The spectrum is subject to two natural upper bounds, whose extremal cases lead respectively to $r$-maximum character spectrum ($r$-MCS) and $r$-full character spectrum ($r$-FCS) systems. We establish the existence of $r$-FCS systems in a broad parameter range, and solve the size-constrained extremal problem completely when $r=k-1$, including the minimum-cost multiplicity profiles. For $1\le r<k$, put $M_r=\qbinom{k}{r}$ and $B_r=\qbinom{k-1}{r}$. The minimum size $ν_r(k,q)$ of an $r$-MCS system satisfies \[\left\lceil\frac{\binom{M_r}{2}}{B_r}\right\rceil\le ν_r(k,q)\le \binom{M_r-1}{2}+\frac{q^k-q^{k-r}}{q-1}.\] The upper bound is at most $\binom{M_r}{2}$, strictly less when $r\le k-2$, and exact when $r=k-1$. Its proof applies positive additive labelings to the complement of one flat, whose trace is empty while all remaining traces are distinct. For $r=1$, we improve the known upper bounds on the minimum length of such systems. We also develop global moment identities and local flat-incidence bounds that impose strong structural constraints on large character spectra. Under the projective-system correspondence, complementary character spectra are the support-weight spectra of $r$-dimensional subcodes.

papers.title: Anomalies of TQFTs coupled to parameter spaces and constraints on ground-state degeneracies
papers.abstract: Anomalies of global symmetries can arise in long-range entangled quantum many-body systems and provide useful constraints on their dynamics. In this paper, we study anomalies of $d$-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) coupled to parameter spaces and their implications for ground-state degeneracies. Specifically, we formulate anomalies as obstructions to constructing parametrized families of TQFTs. We discuss how the classification of these anomalies depends on the choice of topology on the universal $\mathrm{U}(1)$ $(d-1)$-form symmetry. In this framework, we use the projective ground-state bundle obtained by compactifying the TQFT on a spatial manifold to derive a general constraint relating its ground-state degeneracy $N$ to its torsion anomaly $ω$, expressed as $N\int_Wω\in\mathbb{Z}$ for bundles $W$ of spatial manifolds over closed surfaces. We apply this constraint to ground-state degeneracies of (2+1)-dimensional TQFTs with framing and 1-form symmetry anomalies and to obstructions to symmetry-preserving TQFTs. We also discuss implications for bordism generators and propose a conjecture on anomaly detection by manifolds fibered over surfaces.

papers.title: Gearbox cavities: Ultrahigh wave confinement via broken rotational symmetry
papers.abstract: Cavity enhancement of emission from a point source typically relies on structures that preserve its cylindrical symmetry, such as circular Bragg gratings. Combining inverse design with fundamental limits, we show that breaking this symmetry is necessary to maximize the local density of states in lossless two-dimensional cavities. Symmetry-broken designs exceed limits over all cylindrically symmetric structures by up to eight orders of magnitude, acting as ``gearboxes'' that convert the source's emission into high-angular-momentum waves trapped behind a centrifugal barrier.

papers.title: On Statistical-Computational Gaps in Graph Combinatorial Testing Problems
papers.abstract: We study high-dimensional graph combinatorial hypothesis testing problems in which a signal is supported on the edge set of an unknown subgraph drawn from a class invariant under vertex relabeling. For Gaussian observations, we characterize sharp statistical and computational thresholds (at polynomial order) for the signal magnitude required for strong detection across various combinatorial graph alternatives. Our analysis is based on bounding the second moments of the full and low-degree likelihood ratios in terms of the overlap of two independent latent structures and comparing the resulting lower bounds with scan, average, and coordinatewise maximum tests. Under an appropriate low-degree conjecture for computational hardness, we obtain planted-clique thresholds matching those known for Gaussian submatrix detection and identify new statistical-computational gaps for multiple planted cliques and hypercliques, thick cycles and thick paths. We also establish a novel transfer principle across natural exponential family observation models: matching the one-coordinate chi-square divergence preserves full likelihood-ratio second moments exactly and makes low-degree second moments equivalent up to constant factors under a degree condition. Under local regularity, we obtain corresponding testing upper bounds in terms of an effective signal strength. When these upper and lower bounds match, they yield universal threshold scales in the local alternative regime. As a consequence, statistical-computational gaps for planted-clique detection in Erdős--Rényi settings can be deduced from the Gaussian model.

papers.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
papers.abstract: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. Therefore, we introduce Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures these parameters before training. DAMI assigns geometric timescales across heads for varied retrieval distances and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers. A small activation sample calibrates the GDN-family implementation to match both behavioral targets without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI improves average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over the corresponding random-initialization baselines. Performance on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remains broadly comparable to those baselines. Our code is available at https://speedai.com/research/dami.

papers.title: Relaxation speed in quenched-random force fields
papers.abstract: Disorder is commonly expected to slow down relaxation, as in glasses and disordered magnets. Here we show that this need not be the case in general, by analysing the asymptotic relaxation rate of a Brownian particle in a harmonic background potential and a quenched-random Gaussian force field with conservative and non-conservative components. Combining weak-disorder perturbation theory, random-matrix theory, and numerical solutions of the Fokker-Planck equation, we show that the outcome depends on the geometry of the background and on the properties of the random forces. We identify two distinct mechanisms that shape the relaxation speed: an effective stiffening of the background by the disorder, as previously reported in one dimension, and interactions (repulsive and attractive) between the levels of the Fokker-Planck operator. Through level attraction, a common feature of non-Hermitian operators, non-conservative driving forces pull the slowest mode towards faster ones, which facilitates faster relaxation. In anisotropic backgrounds, both effects occur at second order in the disorder strength, enabling either slower or faster relaxation. In isotropic backgrounds, level interactions dominate and the disorder affects the degenerate slowest mode already at first order. The shift is then given by the left-most eigenvalue of a Gaussian random matrix and relaxation is generically slowed down. In backgrounds whose anisotropy is comparable to the disorder strength, level attraction is most effective by merging the slowest mode with its neighbour into an oscillating complex-conjugate pair. In this case, relaxation becomes faster on average once the random forces are sufficiently non-conservative. Our results draw a nuanced picture of how disorder affects the asymptotic relaxation speed in complex systems and uncover general mechanisms that are likely to apply beyond the current setting.

papers.title: Solvable coupled cluster states in $d=\infty$ with prescribed momentum distribution
papers.abstract: Two of the most successful ideas in many-body theory, the exponential coupled cluster ansatz and DMFT, have to date developed separately. We establish a connection between them, by showing that the infinite dimensional limit of the hypercubic lattice allows the exact closed-form evaluation of static expectation values of coupled cluster wave functions, provided the cluster amplitudes admit a low-rank decomposition. As a result, evaluation errors -- a serious concern in conventional coupled cluster theory -- can be disentangled from limitations to expressivity of coupled cluster states. For this family of coupled cluster states, the cavity construction in $d\to\infty$ exactly reduces the environment of a lattice site to a Gaussian Grassmann kernel, and irreducible diagrams for one-body expectation values are found to be site-diagonal (in analogy to the DMFT self-energy). The resulting ``impurity problem" is an integral over a finite number of Grassmann variables rather than a dynamical quantum impurity problem, so that static observables derive exactly from a static self-consistency condition: a wave function counterpart of DMFT. For the simplest case of a cluster amplitude restricted to rank-one doubles, we obtain the momentum distribution in closed form. We show that any momentum distribution can be realized by a state that is the exact and unique ground state of an explicit parent Hamiltonian with a gapless single-particle tunnelling spectrum. By construction these coupled cluster states variationally recover low order perturbation theory for the Hubbard model. Their failure in the strong coupling regime near the Mott transition diagnoses a fundamental limitation of coupled cluster doubles. Intriguingly, our family of coupled cluster wave functions includes a gapless state with zero quasiparticle weight, with a momentum distribution that is completely smooth at the Fermi energy.

papers.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
papers.abstract: World-action models increasingly apply test-time scaling, spending extra inference computation on candidate selection and adaptive allocation to improve control. Such gains are credible only when candidates carry exploitable signal, nominal compute savings become real speedup, and evaluation stays reliable. We audit all three on Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa with a premise-first, pre-registered methodology. On clean data, a learned value selector is 1.66 pp worse than random; a hindsight oracle gains only 1.40 pp, with an episode-level interval spanning zero; and 82% of states show identical candidate outcomes, leaving little selection headroom. Token pruning cuts per-forward FLOPs by up to 47% but yields at most a measured 1.15$\times$ end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.25$\times$ on a decode-excluded path), short of a 1.5$\times$ target, and our adaptive-allocation experiment is inconclusive under a power gate. We further identify and fix a silent rendering corruption whose rate rises sharply along compute-heavy planning paths while leaving the official direct-policy result unaffected, and release a detector, fix, and scripts. These findings show why test-time scaling should be audited as a chain of premises (decision signal, realized efficiency, evaluationintegrity) rather than by success rate alone. Conclusions are scoped to the tested configuration.

papers.title: Microswimmers lose by swimming selfishly
papers.abstract: At low Reynolds number, microswimmers are coupled by the flows they create, even when they are apart. The best way for each swimmer to push itself forward then depends on its neighbors, turning swimming together into a game. To study this, we optimize the shape changes of soft swimmers, alone and in pairs, with a differentiable Stokes solver. From random initial membrane motions, a lone swimmer converges to a traveling membrane wave. In a pair, the stroke of a swimmer affects its neighbor far more than the neighbor affects its own best stroke. For swimmers in line, this influence decays as $1/\ell$ with their separation $\ell$, whereas the incentive to respond decays as $1/\ell^2$. Selfish swimmers, which maximize their own payoff, respond only to the weak incentive. The cooperative gain they miss decays only as $1/\ell^2$, and their selfish adaptations leave the pair worse off than if both had kept their solitary strokes. Related swimmers, which also value the payoff of their neighbor, recover this gain, whereas competitors pay to hinder each other, both following a law that we derive analytically. Hydrodynamics alone thus makes swimming in company a social dilemma, whose outcome depends on how much the swimmers value each other.

papers.title: Neutrino Oscillation in a Static Dihole Geometry
papers.abstract: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the static equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole geometry, restricting the propagation to the symmetry plane. Within the null approximation, we derive the leading contribution to the neutrino phase and numerically evaluate the geodesic integrals. For two neutrino flavors, interference between different trajectories introduces a dependence on the individual neutrino masses and on the neutrino mass ordering for nonmaximal mixing. We analyze the transition probability in different spacetime configurations possessing two light rings, a merged light ring (critical configuration), and no light rings in the equatorial plane. In the weak-lensing regime, the transition probability generally increases with the black holes' individual masses, while variations in the half-separation produce no qualitative change in the transition probability. In stronger-lensing configurations, variations in both the mass and half-separation modify the heights and positions of the extrema, with no monotonic increase or decrease in the transition probability. For the critical and no-light-ring configurations studied, we identify three zero-winding trajectories connecting the source and detector, including one passing near the symmetry axis. The probability remains oscillatory, and its oscillatory pattern depends strongly on the neutrino energy.

papers.title: WASABI: Wasserstein Sampling via Bridge Interpolants
papers.abstract: Sampling from Boltzmann distributions is a fundamental problem in physics, chemistry, and biology. We introduce WAsserstein SAmpling via Bridge Interpolants (WASABI), a method that trains a diffusion model to generate samples from a target Boltzmann distribution given access only to the energy function. WASABI minimizes the KL divergence between the distribution generated by its diffusion model and the Boltzmann target using Wasserstein gradient flows. This approach builds on a principle underlying classical sampling methods such as Langevin dynamics. However, applying Wasserstein gradient flows to diffusion models is challenging because the updates require the gradient of the model's own log density, which is generally intractable. We derive a practical training algorithm that avoids computing this gradient. Once trained, WASABI can generate new samples without further evaluations of the energy or its gradient. On alanine dipeptide, WASABI outperforms the best reported baselines using an estimated 3.3 times fewer energy evaluations. It also achieves competitive performance on interacting particle system benchmarks.

papers.title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting with uncertainty quantification is critical in a variety of scientific applications ranging from epidemiology and economics to energy systems and earth sciences. Yet most forecasting models still need to be developed and trained separately for each domain-specific dataset. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) aim to remove this limitation and enable the application of the same model across domains through large-scale pretraining. However, most existing TSFMs treat each time series independently and therefore cannot model interactions among time series and external drivers. Here, we introduce Chronos-2, a foundation model for zero-shot forecasting that models the interactions between multivariate time series and heterogeneous covariates, which commonly arise in scientific applications. The model infers relationships among time series directly from historical context and generates probabilistic forecasts without task-specific treatment. Across various benchmarks, Chronos-2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on average by improving skill scores by 5.2 percentage points relative to the strongest baselines and increasing win rates by 10 percentage points. Chronos-2 is also computationally efficient, generating forecasts for 100 time series in under one second on a single mid-range GPU, 50x and 1000x faster end-to-end than the best task-specific point and probabilistic forecasters, respectively. In addition, we demonstrate its effectiveness in diverse scientific settings -- including infectious-disease forecasting, macroeconomic modeling, carbon-flux prediction, and runoff simulation -- where the model matches or surpasses specialized methods developed for each domain. These results show that a single pretrained model can capture structure shared across temporal systems.

papers.title: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant. Our results show that the observational tension encountered in the minimal quartic double-well model need not extend to topological inflation in a minimal multi-natural axion potential.

papers.title: Thermal conductivity of Lennard-Jones fluids from equilibrium thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We derive a general expression for the thermal conductivity of simple fluids within a thermodynamic transport theory (TTT) in which the Onsager coefficients of an interacting system are related to those of an ideal reference system through the ratio of the determinants of the Hessians of the relevant thermodynamic potential. The transported quantity is identified with an effective energy density proportional to the rms energy fluctuations of a small fluid cell. The result expresses the thermal conductivity as the product of its dilute-gas value and a function of equilibrium thermodynamic properties, namely the specific heats at constant density and at constant $ρT$ and the temperature derivative of the latter, with no adjustable parameters. For hard spheres, it reduces to a previously verified expression in terms of the thermodynamic factor. The theory is tested against molecular dynamics results for the Lennard-Jones (LJ) and the truncated and shifted Lennard-Jones (LJTS) fluids in the supercritical region, for densities up to $ρ^*=0.8$, using equations of state based on perturbation theory. For the LJTS fluid, the mean absolute percentage error is below 8\% for all the temperatures considered. For the LJ fluid, the predictions are compared with those of the revised Enskog theory for Mie fluids, using the same equation of state: TTT gives smaller errors at almost all temperatures, with a significant improvement at low temperatures, where the errors are reduced approximately by a factor between two and three.

papers.title: Cosmology with post-EoR 21 cm Intensity Mapping surveys: power spectrum measurements in the last decade
papers.abstract: The technique of 21 cm intensity mapping (IM) is emerging as a possible, cost-effective method to supplement optical surveys to map the large-scale structure, and extend their redshift reach, with projects aiming to cover a large range of post-EoR redshifts, from z=0 to z=6. Since the early discussions 20 years ago, a few dedicated interferometers have been built, and surveys have been carried out using them as well as general purpose radio instruments. An introduction to late-time cosmology with 21 cm intensity mapping is given, highlighting the main scientific and technical challenges. We present then an overview of different instrument concepts and survey strategies, followed by a discussion of outstanding data analysis challenges, most notably the foreground subtraction, which is a major issue in IM. We carry on with a presentation of the currently active projects and the 21 cm signal measurements which have been obtained, either in cross-correlation with optical surveys, or as the autocorrelation power spectrum. Finally, we discuss briefly the prospects for this field with future instruments and surveys such as SKA, HIRAX and CHORD.

papers.title: The Prior-Force Family of Implicit Denoiser Priors and Its Decisions in Linear Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Implicit priors given by Gaussian denoisers successfully regularize a wide range of inverse problems in approaches such as plug-and-play (PnP), regularization by denoising (RED) and score-based methods. Such a prior depends on the noise level, and how it selects among signals consistent with the data remains largely uncharacterized. To put implicit and explicit priors on the same footing, we define the prior-force family $W_t=t^{-1}(D_t^{-1}-I)$ of any Gaussian denoiser $D_t$ at noise variance $t>0$ (inverse in the graph sense), the normalized denoising residual as an operator on clean signals. At a common effective prior weight, the equilibrium equations differ only in their prior terms: PnP uses $W_t$, RED/score-based methods the score force (the normalized residual as an operator on noisy inputs), and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation the MAP force (the negative log-prior gradient). For the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) denoisers of a prior $π$, we compare the corresponding energies at three levels. Without observation, raising the noise level favors PnP minima that retain more posterior variance. On signals consistent with the data, the leading-order PnP energy for separated modes is the proximal hull of the MAP energy, which lets PnP select signals between modes; modes of equal data fit are ranked by peak height at small noise levels and by mass at large ones. For recovery, $W_t$ at the truth bounds the local bias, and an oracle noise level balances this bias against denoiser error. These results show that the noise level is a parameter of the prior rather than a step size. Experiments with exact priors support these predictions, including the mixture components that PnP selects on unseen data.

papers.title: Lifting the mixed to the pure: quantum phases of matter from canonical purification
papers.abstract: Pure-state quantum phases are defined through finite-depth local unitary connections. This concept of phases has recently been generalized to mixed states in terms of locally reversible channels. In this work, we establish a fundamental relation between mixed-state phases and pure-state phases. We show that a locally reversible channel between mixed states can be lifted to a local isometry between their canonical purifications; thus, if two mixed states are in the same phase, then their canonical purifications are in the same pure-state phase. Furthermore, an explicit construction of the lifting isometry is given by ``half'' of the Petz recovery map, suggesting that the Petz recovery map \emph{without rotation} is enough to connect mixed state phases. We illustrate our results with two examples: toric code under bit flip noise and Chern insulator under fermion number noise.

papers.title: Focusing through coupled multimode fibers for miniaturized single-atom tweezer arrays
papers.abstract: Real-world deployment of quantum technologies requires systems in low SWaP-C packages. Quantum platforms based on ultracold atoms typically trap and control atoms with optical tweezers using light focused through bulky objective lenses, which are costly and sensitive to misalignment. Multimode fibers (MMFs) offer a compact route to focusing light, but their use in forming optical tweezers for cold atoms has been limited to a single fiber. Here we use a 2x1 MMF fused coupler to obtain two independent control paths sharing a common distal facet. We form near-diffraction-limited tweezers through each channel, suppress interference by applying a small frequency offset between the channels, and demonstrate that the tweezer separation is insensitive to misalignment of the input coupling. This work provides a route to reconfigurable single-atom arrays in low SWaP-C environments.

papers.title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance in a Bilayer Graphene Quantum Point Contact
papers.abstract: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 $μ$V, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. For in-plane fields, the enhancement persists up to the critical field, and the bias window follows the spectral gap predicted by Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.

papers.title: Two-loop matter power spectrum from FFTLog and kite integrals
papers.abstract: We present a fast and accurate method for computing the two-loop matter power spectrum in the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFTofLSS). Using FFTLog, we decompose the linear power spectrum into complex power laws, reducing the two-loop corrections to cosmology-independent massless Feynman integrals of kite topology. A central numerical challenge is the evaluation of these integrals for complex powers with large imaginary parts, where the highly oscillatory integrands make accurate numerical evaluation particularly challenging. We overcome this difficulty using a Mellin--Barnes representation summed over a uniform lattice, achieving approximately ten digit precision even for large imaginary powers, with an error estimate for each integral. The resulting precomputed matrices allow the two-loop power spectrum to be evaluated for a new cosmology in a few milliseconds. Comparing with direct numerical integration, we find agreement at the $10^{-4}$ level relative to the power spectrum up to $k=0.2$ $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ after accounting for EFTofLSS counterterm contributions and FFTLog decomposition errors. The same framework extends to biased tracers and redshift-space distortions, providing the building blocks for general two-loop calculations in EFTofLSS. We make the code for evaluating the kite integrals publicly available, together with precomputed matrices and an implementation for the two-loop matter power spectrum as a concrete application. Our results can be directly incorporated into existing FFTLog-based codes for large-scale structure, extending their current one-loop capabilities to two loops within the same computational framework.

papers.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) embodies a foundational paradigm for sequential decision-making in the face of uncertainty. The rapid growth of model complexity in emerging applications has significantly amplified the challenges of achieving data-efficient RL, particularly in sample-starved scenarios where data collection may be costly, time-consuming, or even high-stakes. Consequently, understanding and improving the data efficiency of RL algorithms has become a central problem of both fundamental theoretical interest and practical importance. Despite decades of research, the statistical underpinnings of RL remained remarkably underdeveloped until relatively recently, particularly in the finite-sample regimes most relevant to modern practice. Over the past few years, there has been a surge of activity advancing the frontiers of non-asymptotic statistical RL theory, drawing on ideas from high-dimensional statistics and probability, information theory, and statistical learning theory. In this monograph, we present a non-asymptotic treatment for RL based on tabular Markov decision processes, focusing on three canonical sampling mechanisms --- RL with a generative model, online RL, and offline RL --- together with two algorithmic paradigms: model-based and model-free approaches. Centered around non-asymptotic sample complexity analysis, our treatment emphasizes minimax-optimal algorithm design, particularly methods that attain statistical optimality without significant burn-in costs, as well as sharp statistical characterizations of several widely used RL algorithms. Whenever possible, we provide largely self-contained analyses together with intuitive explanations. We also briefly discuss several extensions, such as robust RL, competitive multi-agent RL, federated RL, uncertainty quantification, and RL from human feedback.

papers.title: On approximate support versions of Donoho--Stark uncertainty principles for $k$-Hadamard operators
papers.abstract: In this paper we present results related to Donoho--Stark type uncertainty principles that were proved in the article "The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme" by Wigderson and Wigderson for $k$-Hadamard operators in the finite-dimensional setting. Namely, the authors showed that Donoho-Stark principles can be generalized to versions for approximate supports with respect to norms $\ell^{p}$ for $p=1$ and $p=2$. In the second case they assumed the so-called speciality condition, namely that a suitable matrix satisfies $A^{*}A = kI$. First we show that such theorems cannot be generalized to $p>1$ if matrices are not special $k$-Hadamard. Next we prove Donoho-Stark type principle for special $k$-Hadamard operators for $\ell^{p}$ norms within the range $1\leq p\leq 2$. Finally, we show that such theorems are false for $p>2$ even in the presence of the speciality condition.

papers.title: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ Spin-1/2 Qubits
papers.abstract: Scaling silicon spin qubits to fault-tolerant processors requires semiconductor foundry integration, yet it remains unclear how industrial fabrication and dense device integration affect qubit control and noise. Here we study ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ electron spin-1/2 qubits fabricated using Intel's industry-compatible 300 mm process and incorporating micromagnets for electrically driven spin resonance, using a high-performance device fabricated in the RIKEN research cleanroom as a reference. Primitive $π/2$-gate fidelities reach the 99.99% level in the Intel devices, which also exhibit longer idle coherence, weaker low-frequency correlations and reduced qubit-to-qubit variability across several measured characteristics. In the present Intel devices, the micromagnets are integrated inline with the back-end-of-line (BEOL) contact routing, with their separation from the quantum well set through the vertical stack design. Relative to the reference, their larger separation contributes to weaker longitudinal and transverse magnetic-field gradients. The weaker longitudinal gradient suppresses the conversion of charge noise into qubit-frequency fluctuations, whereas the weaker transverse gradient reduces electrically driven spin-resonance efficiency and makes drive-dependent errors relevant at lower Rabi frequencies. Additional BEOL routing and metal levels required for two-dimensional arrays make such placement decisions increasingly consequential when scaling. These results establish an integration-level control-noise trade-off linking micromagnet placement within densely routed layouts to achievable gate performance, while very high-fidelity operation remains possible in industrially fabricated devices.

papers.title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
papers.abstract: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses. Beyond characterization, nonlocality in multiscale systems is increasingly viewed as a design element across fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems. Existing nonlocality theories provide rigorous descriptions and mechanistic insight, but often require prescribed analytic forms, range, symmetries, or periodicity. Machine learning offers a data-driven route to learn interactions, yet principled approaches that tie the network design to physical theory remain nascent. Here we present domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations from field data alone. Through a case study in large-scale optical metasurfaces, we demonstrate DANO's full-field prediction under geometric heterogeneity and across drive conditions, small-to-large domain transfer, and multifunctional inverse design, with learned interactions validated through physics-based interrogation. As an AI-for-Science tool, it supports interaction discovery and scalable, customizable design of nonlocal multiscale systems, including virtual-reality optics.

papers.title: Numerical evaluation of one-loop integrals using quadrature rules
papers.abstract: We introduce a numerical quadrature algorithm with stretched exponential convergence to evaluate one-loop integrals in dimensional regularisation in the causal Loop Tree Dual (cLTD) representation. The key feature that makes this possible is the fact that for Euclidean kinematics all singularities of the cLTD integrand lie on a compact set in loop momentum space. We prove that our algorithm admits a stretched exponential convergence with the number of integrand evaluations, and we illustrate it by evaluating triangle, box and pentagon integrals at selected Euclidean kinematics points. We benchmark our implementation against analytic results as well as results obtained via Monte Carlo integration. We also provide a proof of concept that our algorithm can be extended to physical kinematics after subtraction of threshold singularities.

papers.title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

papers.title: Rates and Nearly-Lossless State over a Multi-Access Channel with Causal State Information
papers.abstract: The problem of transmitting both data and state over a memoryless state-dependent multi-access channel with causal state information is addressed. The state comprises three independent components: a common component, which is revealed to both en- coders, and two private components, each of which is revealed to a different encoder. The data are to be recovered with arbitrarily-small probability of error, and the state sequence with arbitrarily-small symbol-error rate. Under the assumption that the capacity region in the absence of a state recon- struction constraint is nonempty, the capacity region is derived and is shown to be achievable using a Block-Markov coding scheme employing binning and superposition coding.

papers.title: Batch Universal Prediction via Conditional Additive Smoothing
papers.abstract: Modern language models motivate renewed interest in universal prediction problems in which a predictor can exploit previously observed data before predicting a fresh sequence. We study an idealized version of this setting by introducing \emph{batch regret}: a conditional analogue of classical average regret in which a predictor observes a batch of $n$ training sequences and is then evaluated on an independent test sequence generated by the same unknown source. Additive smoothing estimators, which add a bias to the observed token frequencies before predicting the next token, played a fundamental role as a simple prediction strategy with almost-optimal average regret for memoryless and Markov sources. Their equivalent under batch regret are the conditional additive smoothing estimators, which estimate the conditional distribution of the test sequence given the training batch. In this work, we study their asymptotical batch regret for binary memoryless and first-order Markov sources. For binary memoryless sources, we show how the optimal bias of the estimator, and consequently the corresponding batch regret, change as a function of the training batch size $n$, by extending the Poisson-based analysis of Krichevsky. For binary Markov sources with positive transitions, we characterize the leading coefficient of batch regret and its dependence on whether the initial law is known, free, or stationary. Finally, we introduce a Rényi analogue of batch regret and identify the corresponding optimal predictors as conditional $α$-NML estimators, thereby giving an operational interpretation to a conditional version of Sibson's $α$-mutual information.

papers.title: Channel dichotomies
papers.abstract: We study channel interconversion under non-signalling superchannels, where the asymptotic conversion rate is given by the ratio of the channel capacities. Our main result determines the second-order expansion of the optimal target length. Namely, when each channel has a single capacity-achieving dispersion, the coefficient is given by the inverse sesquinormal distribution, with parameters determined by the capacities and dispersions. The result extends state-dichotomy theory to channels: one superchannel approximates the target uniformly over inputs and maps every reference channel whose output is independent of its input to another such channel. As in state dichotomies, there are finite-error resonances where the second-order term vanishes, leaving an $O(\log n)$ remainder. Crucially, our new characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols [Cao {\it et al.}~IEEE Trans.~Inf.~Theory (2024)]. Instead, the proof combines comparisons of binary hypothesis testing experiments with uniform Gaussian estimates and a construction that uses symmetry within type classes to satisfy the non-signalling constraints. Shared randomness assistance already suffices at first order, but we show that its second-order behaviour can differ strictly from the non-signalling case.

papers.title: Creating functional nanostructures for vortex manipulation in superconducting Bi$_\text{2}$Sr$_\text{2}$CaCu$_\text{2}$O$_\text{8+x}$ thin films via focused He ion beam irradiation
papers.abstract: Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) is a highly anisotropic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting unique vortex dynamics due to its layered structure. Precise nanoscale patterning of ultrathin Bi-2212 films remains challenging, limiting controlled studies of vortex pinning. Here, we employ 30 keV focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation to fabricate periodic arrays of columnar defects with 100 nm spacings in optimally-doped Bi-2212 thin films, thereby creating artificial vortex pinning centers. Magnetotransport measurements reveal pronounced vortex matching effects, evidenced by minima in magnetoresistance and peaks in critical current at commensurate magnetic fields. The angular dependence of magnetoresistance and critical current scale with an effective magnetic field, indicating strong confinement of pancake vortices along irradiation-induced tracks. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of He-FIB nanopatterning in modulating the superconducting properties in Bi-2212 thin films, providing a platform for fundamental studies of vortex matter and advancing prospects for device applications based on this highly anisotropic superconductor.

papers.title: Primordial black holes and gravitational waves from aligned axion inflation
papers.abstract: We study the production of primordial black holes (PBHs) and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) in aligned axion inflation through the transition between two stages of inflation. The first stage proceeds along a metastable trajectory and ends when this trajectory loses stability, causing the fields to turn towards the attractor of the second inflationary stage. During the transition, coupled adiabatic--entropy evolution produces a localized enhancement of the curvature power spectrum. We compute the PBH abundance from this spectrum assuming Gaussian primordial curvature perturbations and using the nonlinear compaction-function formalism with a spectrum-dependent collapse threshold and critical collapse. Representative benchmark solutions yield asteroid-mass PBHs with a potentially significant dark-matter abundance, together with an associated SIGW background.

papers.title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
papers.abstract: We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large. This threshold is information-theoretically optimal for the symmetric two-community model and is conjectured to mark the limit of efficient recovery in broader symmetric models. Our result matches the recovery guarantees of non-backtracking spectral methods while using Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices. To do this, we identify recursive formulas for the negative outlier eigenvalues and show that their eigenspaces have nonvanishing overlap with the corresponding planted eigenspaces. The proof constructs approximate eigenvectors from the planted labels on the limiting Poisson tree, with weights given by its Green's function, and transfers these approximations to the finite graph.

papers.title: A new upper bound for $A(19,6,8)$
papers.abstract: We compute Polak's bound $A_4(19,6,8)$ for binary constant weight codes, obtaining the numerical value $673.04001$. An exact rational certificate gives $A_4(19,6,8)\le 673.0400143064802474039375132665301315202504$, and hence $A(19,6,8)\le 673$. This improves the upper bound $693$ listed in Brouwer's table. The certificate is verified by a separate program using exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: The Dynamical Mass Profiles of Galaxy Groups - Application to IllustrisTNG-300
papers.abstract: We present a new rescaling and stacking method to test cold dark matter predictions through the dynamical modelling of galaxy groups using the Jeans equation. We test the viability of this method on idealised, line-of-sight group data at $z=0$ in the IllustrisTNG-300 simulation, using subhalos and satellite galaxies as tracers. Dynamical mass profiles are measured using the code `Gravsphere' for seven distinct quality cuts, three on the dark matter substructure and four on the `visible' satellite galaxies. When using the dark matter substructure, we find that selecting subhalos by their infall time onto the group provides the best recovery of the true mass profile. When using satellite galaxies we instead find that selecting quenched satellites provides the best recovery. In both cases the mass profile is recovered within $<1σ$ of the true value up to $\sim 1.5$ times the median host virial radius. However, we also find the recovered velocity anisotropy to be biased towards negative values for all seven of our subhalo samples beyond the median host virial radius. This suggests dynamical systematics may still be present in the data, which will need to be quantified in future work before application to surveys.

papers.title: From thermogravity to thermocosmology with a running non-conservation scale
papers.abstract: Thermogravity offers a novel approach to cosmic acceleration, deriving trace-free gravitational equations and matter non-conservation from thermodynamic processes in spacetime. We extend this framework towards thermocosmology by introducing a running non-conservation scale $L_2(H)$, while restricting non-conservation to cold dark matter. We investigate two prescriptions, namely a Hubble-proportional rate and an inverse-Hubble running model, deriving their cosmological dynamics and effective geometric dark-energy description. The first admits an exact analytical solution and is related to quadratic running-vacuum cosmologies, while the second approaches standard matter dilution at early times and allows reversals in the direction of energy exchange. Interestingly, the reconstructed geometric dark energy can exhibit quintessence-like and phantom-like behavior, including smooth crossings of the phantom divide, without introducing a phantom field or superacceleration. A unified dynamical-system analysis reveals distinct matter-era critical configurations and a continuous family of de Sitter solutions that are transversely attracting under suitable conditions. Confronting both models with Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, we find a mild preference for positive present-day matter non-conservation. The Akaike information criterion slightly favors the thermogravity scenarios, whereas the Bayesian information criterion favors the simpler $Λ$CDM model. Thus, running thermocosmology provides a viable framework for nontrivial effective dark-energy dynamics.

papers.title: Characterizations and MacWilliams-Like Identities of Weakly Regular Bent Partitions
papers.abstract: Bent partitions play a significant role in the theory of bent functions. In this paper, we study weakly regular bent partitions, that is, all generated bent functions are weakly regular (called in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$). Let $Γ=\{A_{i}, i \in V_{m}\}$ be a bent partition of $V_{n}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$, where $V_{n}$ denotes an $n$-dimensional vector space over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_{p}$, $n$ is even, $m \leq \frac{n}{2}$, and $m \geq 2$ if $p=2$. We first characterize bent partition $Γ$ in terms of the duals of component functions of vectorial bent functions. In particular, we prove that if $p \neq 3$, then all bent functions generated by $Γ$ are regular. Building on the above result, we give characterizations of bent partition $Γ$ in terms of two classes of linear codes. When $n \geq 4$ and $m=\frac{n}{2}$, except for the case where $(p, n)=(2, 4)$ and $|A_{i_{0}}|=1$ for some $i_{0}$, we show that $Γ$ is obtained from a spread (after a shift). Particularly, any normal bent partition of $V_{n}$ of depth $p^{\frac{n}{2}}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$ must be obtained from a spread (after a shift), where $n \geq 4$. We establish the Macwilliams-like identities for bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$. Furthermore, if $p$ is odd, we present some nonexistence results on bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$.

papers.title: Homogeneous Spectral Freedom and Hadamard Consistency of Perturbative Green Functions
papers.abstract: Perturbative mode equations often admit formally different particular solutions whose spectral sums appear to have different short-distance singularities. We formulate a general diagnostic which separates this representational freedom from a genuine change of quantum state: for a fixed normally hyperbolic operator, two Hadamard two-point functions can differ only by a smooth homogeneous bisolution. Thus, a nonsmooth term generated by rearranging a perturbative source must be traced either to a changed operator or to inadmissible homogeneous spectral data. We apply the criterion to two impulsive plane-wave backgrounds. Starting directly from the metrics, we recompute the wave operators, modes, world functions, and Van Vleck determinants. Exact-mode matching and the geometrical construction agree through second order for the first profile. In the second, correcting the metric changes the leading perturbation from quadratic to linear order in the wave parameter and eliminates inverse transverse-momentum poles, while the corrected metric retains an exact aligned null-radiation Einstein source. In both examples the singular Green function is precisely the perturbative expansion of the Hadamard parametrix; the additional logarithms arise from momentum-singular homogeneous data. For the exactly soluble first profile, the standard flat-normalized plane-wave prescription gives a vanishing renormalized stress tensor away from the impulsive surface. Smooth-front regularizations of both profiles reproduce, at the calculated orders and away from the characteristic zero mode, the singular structure of the matched impulsive propagators without generating inverse transverse-momentum poles.

papers.title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
papers.abstract: The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron. Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.

papers.title: Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT
papers.abstract: Reusing the Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) common stream for sensing eliminates dedicated probing signals in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), but creates a feasibility bottleneck: the common-power fraction must simultaneously support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection. This paper investigates this tradeoff in downlink zero-forcing RSMA with imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). With the common beam fixed over a sensing dwell through sensing geometry, the common-power fraction becomes the sole design variable. We prove that the communication-feasible set is either a closed interval or empty. Analytical outage expressions localize these endpoints, revealing a high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) floor-ceiling effect: common decoding dictates a common-power floor, while imperfect CSIT and SIC impose a private-decoding ceiling. For sensing, the conditional detection constraint is affine, preserving the interval structure. A geometry-matched common beam ensures monotonic detection improvement, reducing joint-feasibility check to the communication-feasible upper endpoint. Simulations validate our analysis, identifying regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.

papers.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
papers.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.

papers.title: Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments
papers.abstract: Reliable evaluation of AI agents for table-top science experiments has remained elusive because live instruments are hard to reset and share at scale, while instrument statefulness and safety constraints complicate evaluation. We introduce instrMCP and q-devBench, an evaluation stack for instrument-centered AI agents in table-top experiments. instrMCP connects coding agents to scientific instruments through the Model Context Protocol, serving as the instrument-access harness. q-devBench reconstructs 37 real experimental tasks from condensed-matter physics as virtual QCoDeS instruments covering quantum electronic transport, scanning probe imaging, and calibration workflows. q-devBench exposes reproducible failure modes in laboratory-agent systems while preserving realistic instrument-control workflows. Across a range of commercial coding-agent configurations, current systems already show substantial operational competence, satisfying 70-83% of measurement-related rubric criteria. The main bottleneck is scientific analysis, where performance falls to 28-46%. In an analysis-only ablation in which agents receive clean reference datasets without running the virtual measurement session, analysis performance improves substantially, closing roughly two thirds of the difference between the measurement and analysis scores. This suggests that much of the deficit arises from the measurement-session context, including tool-use overhead, longer context, measurement-planning decisions, and possible acquisition errors, while a residual scientific-reasoning gap remains. Together, instrMCP and q-devBench provide a practical sandbox for benchmarking, diagnosing, and improving laboratory AI harnesses, and establish a route from controlled virtual evaluation to future live-hardware validation.

papers.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
papers.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

papers.title: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
papers.abstract: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit. The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.

papers.title: Pair density waves via interband pairing --- a perspective from superfluid weight
papers.abstract: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.

papers.title: Secure Deterministic Identification with Feedback and Sensing over State-Dependent Wiretap Channels
papers.abstract: Identification differs from classical transmission in that the receiver determines whether a particular identity was sent rather than recovering a message. We study secure deterministic identification over state-dependent discrete memoryless wiretap channels with private noiseless feedback and a sensing distortion constraint. The encoder has no local randomness and uses only the identity and past feedback. A symbol-wise input restriction guarantees the sensing constraint. We show that the secure deterministic identification capacity equals its non-secure feedback counterpart when the admissible main channel has positive ordinary transmission capacity and H(Y|Z,X=x)>0 for some fixed admissible input x. This equality does not require positive classical wiretap secrecy capacity. For achievability, noiseless feedback generates common randomness for identification and enables secret-key extraction by privacy amplification. The extracted key one-time-pad encrypts a short identification tag, whose reliable transmission requires only a sublinear number of additional channel uses. We also present an alternative construction in which feedback-generated randomness replaces the local randomization of a stochastic wiretap encoder. We further prove that secure identification capacity vanishes whenever non-secure identification capacity is zero. We also identify a class of channels with input-independent wiretapper observations that achieves full non-secure identification capacity even when the private conditional feedback entropy is zero, illustrated by a binary state-dependent wiretap channel. Thus, feedback can support both identification and secrecy without local encoder randomization while satisfying sensing constraints.

papers.title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term
papers.abstract: We study the rapid-turn regime of multifield cosmology coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. We derive the corresponding modified relations between the inflationary Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, in the two-field case. These relations show that including the Gauss-Bonnet coupling broadens the possibilities for realizing rapid turn inflation and for satisfying the swampland conjectures. We also derive a consistency condition relating the scalar field-space metric to the scalar potential and the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, which two-field slow-roll and rapid-turn inflationary solutions have to satisfy. Finally, we find general conditions under which phantom-like behavior is possible in multifield dark energy models coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. Notably, although we do not consider a direct interaction between dark matter and dark energy, dark matter is crucial for the occurrence of a phantom regime.

papers.title: An approximate separation of the electron and positron degrees of freedom in the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism
papers.abstract: Here we study the quantum relativistic phase-space description of the Dirac field referred to as the Dirac--Heisenberg--Wigner (DHW) formalism. By applying a systematic expansion procedure in weak electromagnetic fields (compared to the Schwinger critical field) and slow temporal and long spatial scales (compared to the Compton scales), the 16 scalar phase-space functions of the DHW equations can be reduced to 8 scalars. By making a further change of variables, the equations can be interpreted as four evolution equations for the electron degrees of freedom and four for the positron degrees of freedom. We refer to these equations as the weakly coupled electron-positron (WCEP) limit of the DHW equations. Unlike the case after a Foldy--Wouthuysen transformation has been made, the electron and positron degrees of freedom remain weakly coupled. Naturally, further approximations can be made on the 4+4 equations so that only 4 equations for one particle species remain. Importantly, the expansion scheme can be carried out to all orders, in which case the reduced 4+4 model, contrary to other reduced models, will cover most quantum relativistic effects. Specifically, this includes vacuum polarization, a phenomenon that otherwise has been added phenomenologically, but here appears naturally as a feature of the general expansion scheme.

papers.title: Counting kinks and magnons with the lattice: magnetoelastic effects in Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$
papers.abstract: We report low-temperature dilatometry and ultrasound measurements on the frustrated quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$ across the entire cascade of field-induced magnetic phase transitions. The whole phase diagram can be recovered from these lattice probes, with distinct anomalies observed at each phase boundary. Elongation along the principal chain axis is found to closely track magnetization throughout the phase diagram. This behavior is interpreted in terms of kinks in the Néel structure and magnons in the transverse-ordered magnetic-BEC phases, each carrying a fixed lattice distortion. A simultaneous analysis of ultrasound and striction data allows us to quantify the strength of magnetoelastic coupling.

papers.title: Static and dynamic density correlations of interacting active Brownian particles
papers.abstract: We develop a stochastic Dean--Kawasaki field theory to predict the static structure factor and collective intermediate scattering function of interacting active Brownian particles. Starting from the microscopic overdamped dynamics, we derive coupled stochastic equations for the density and polarization fields using an angular-moment closure. Gaussian linearization then yields closed analytical expressions for static and dynamic density correlations in terms of propulsion speed, mean number density, interaction potential, translational and rotational diffusivities. The coupling between density and polarization predicts a crossover from exponential relaxation to damped oscillations despite the absence of inertia. For Gaussian-core potential, the predictions contain no fitting parameters. Brownian dynamics simulations show quantitative agreement at low activity and long wavelengths, and reproduce the crossover behaviour. For Weeks--Chandler--Andersen potential, the nonintegrable core makes both the Fourier transform of the potential and the self-interaction correction term in the Dean--Kawasaki field theory ill-defined. We therefore introduce an approximation that replaces the interaction potential with a passive direct-correlation function fitted separately at each density and temperature. This approximation requires no additional activity-dependent fitting parameters.

papers.title: Hierarchy of Electromagnetic Gauge Field Quantum Geometries
papers.abstract: The conventional Bloch quantum geometric tensor (QGT) describes electric-dipole geometry for spatially uniform perturbations and vertical Bloch transitions. We develop a broader framework linking quantum geometry to local and nonlocal electromagnetic response in gauge-field space, placing this tensor within a hierarchy of electric and magnetic multipole quantum geometries. The intrinsic antisymmetric adiabatic response in every electromagnetic channel is a Berry curvature in the space of its conjugate fields. The field-dependent projector uniquely fixes the QGT for that channel, pairing the response curvature with a quantum metric. This construction extends to spatially nonuniform perturbations, whose finite momentum transfer induces nonvertical Bloch transitions. We explicitly construct the current--current QGT connecting Bloch states at $\mathbf{k}\pm\mathbf{q}/2$, providing a unified metric and curvature description of nonlocal current response. In the doubled Brillouin zone, tangential derivatives generate conventional momentum-space QGT multipoles, whereas normal derivatives connect finite-momentum geometry to uniform electric- and magnetic-multipole-pair QGTs. We derive this connection through second order in $\mathbf{q}$. The finite-momentum curvature governs the intrinsic nonlocal Hall response, while an inverse-frequency moment of symmetric optical absorption probes the index-symmetric metric sector.

papers.title: Underdamped Stochastic Optimal Transport with Landauer boundary conditions: machine learning and analytical solution
papers.abstract: Finding optimal transport protocols for underdamped stochastic processes is a difficult yet important problem in control theory. In this paper we develop a direct method, based on machine learning, to find the optimal solution of the problem in the presence of non-linear boundary conditions, including those modelling the Landauer bit-erasure problem. The dynamics is steered from a single-peak to a double-peak distribution in position space, by only acting on a controllable external potential. The problem is highly non-linear, and analytical solutions are not available in general. We benchmark our numerical results with a perturbative expansion, which is expected to hold in a suitable overdamped limit.

papers.title: Finite-time Mpemba crossings with imperfect preparation
papers.abstract: Two preparations evolving under the same thermal Markov generator can reverse their ordering in relative entropy even when the hotter state retains a nonzero slow-mode component. We derive a sufficient finite-time crossing condition for arbitrary finite irreducible reversible systems. The condition compares the preparations' weights in the entire slowest eigenspace, including degeneracies, and gives an explicit upper bound using the separation from the next distinct decay rate. Exact finite-amplitude entropy comparisons also yield all-mode enclosures and bounds based on a retained spectrum with a controlled omitted tail. A preparation-error inequality converts finite-time sign margins into explicit probability tolerances; extensions account for temperature, generator, and stationary-reference uncertainty. We test the bounds on 2000 predefined network draws with four graph families and 4--64 states. There are 86 numerically located crossings, of which 45 satisfy the simple sufficient condition. In a selected eight-state example, retaining two nonstationary modes certifies a crossing before 1.55163, improving a certified slow-sector endpoint of 2.53951; the located crossing is near 1.26943. A reflecting diffusion in an asymmetric potential supplies a separate physical example, with systematic mesh refinement. Independent interval arithmetic certifies selected spectral bounds, finite-grid first crossings, and an entire preparation-temperature rectangle in a three-state benchmark. The theorem does not require exact slow-mode cancellation, while its numerical sharpness and detection coverage remain model dependent. These results concern relative-entropy relaxation and do not predict water-freezing times.

papers.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging
papers.abstract: Physics-informed Gaussian process (GP) methods provide a probabilistic framework for PDE solving.
